Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
The highest-priority current evidence question is to establish whether the newly accepted H140 finding is robust and reasonably specific rather than an incidental co-deletion or batch signal. I therefore register mechanistic follow-ups for MDM2 dependency: MTAP loss in TP53-wildtype cells, and CDKN2A loss among MTAP-intact TP53-wildtype cells. The first asks whether a common 9p21/MTAP deletion context tracks MDM2 dependency; the second asks whether the accepted CDKN2A association can persist when MTAP loss is absent, which would strengthen specificity to CDKN2A rather than broad locus co-deletion. I also register a screen_batch stratification because H140 is large but still discovery-only. These should be interpreted against an approximate MDM2 clinical threshold near 0.027 mean-score units; H140's +0.119 is far above that, so the new probes are mainly for specificity and technical robustness rather than for detecting marginal effects.

I also register two specificity probes for accepted pathway associations. For USP7, TP53 loss is validated as associated with weaker USP7 dependency, implying that p53-pathway intact cells are relatively more USP7-dependent. Testing PTEN loss within TP53-wildtype cells asks whether another tumor-suppressor loss produces a comparable USP7 phenotype. This is not strongly anticipated, but a clear null would support specificity to TP53 status. For STAT3, PTEN loss is validated as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Testing TP53 loss within PTEN-wildtype cells asks whether p53-pathway loss is independently associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, a plausible inflammation or stress-signaling effect but one that should not be assumed because PTEN and TP53 can co-occur.

Finally, I register a conditional EGFR-amplification test among KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma cells. H90 suggested a potentially meaningful positive signed effect in all KRAS-mutant cells, with a signed estimate of +0.053 and a 95% interval +0.004 to +0.103, above the approximate 0.025 EGFR threshold. Squamous KRAS-mutant EGFR-amplified cells were too sparse, so a direct adenocarcinoma stratum may give a more stable view of whether this conditional signal is localized to the dominant histologic subgroup. All proposed comparisons are still observational hypotheses; none should be interpreted as causal mechanisms or external generalization until evidence and independent validation are assessed.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. record.narrative: All estimates are already signed to the claim direction, so positive values support stronger MDM2 dependency for the CDKN2A-loss claims. H143 through H146 are highly reassuring robustness strata of H140: CDKN2A loss among TP53-wildtype cells showed signed effects of +0.113, +0.117, +0.130, and +0.134 under higher Cas9 activity, Avana library, faster proliferation, and higher screen ROC, respectively. Each 95% lower bound was above the MDM2 clinical threshold, so I accept these as clinically meaningful within-stratum dataset associations and close them as robustness probes. H149 is important for specificity: CDKN2A loss retained a signed effect of +0.106 with lower bound +0.063 among TP53-wildtype cells without MTAP loss, supporting that the H140 signal is not solely a broad 9p21 MTAP co-deletion proxy. H147 shows a similar effect in TP53-loss cells, signed +0.111 with lower bound +0.035. I accept this as evidence that CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency in this p53-loss complement as well, but it weakens any interpretation that the H140 association is strictly TP53-wildtype-specific. It should still be read as observational and possibly related to co-deleted loci or p53-pathway context, not as a causal mechanism. H150 in batch_a has a large point estimate, +0.098, and excludes the null, but its lower bound +0.023 is just below the approximate 0.027 threshold, so I do not consider it decisive for clinical meaningfulness; it is left unresolved and closed, while arguing against a gross batch_a-only artifact. H148, MTAP loss alone in TP53-wildtype cells, has a below-threshold point estimate and an interval that includes both null and clinically meaningful positive values, so it remains unresolved and closed as not informative enough to promote MTAP. For specificity probes, H151 rejects PTEN loss as associated with weaker USP7 dependency within TP53-wildtype cells: the signed estimate is opposite the claim and the upper interval is below the USP7 threshold. H152 rejects TP53 loss as associated with stronger STAT3 dependency within PTEN-wildtype cells: the estimate is essentially null and the upper interval is below the STAT3 threshold. H153 and H31 are unresolved: EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma cells is imprecise and below the EGFR threshold, and KRAS mutation among adenocarcinoma cells is small and imprecise with an interval spanning null and meaningful positive effects. Neither establishes a clinically meaningful association, so I defer the EGFR-KRAS-adenocarcinoma probe and close the adenocarcinoma KRAS probe. record.narrative: This exploration prioritizes formal context modification around independently validated dependencies rather than adding weak marginal probes. In the supplied lung-cell-line dataset, a relative 10 percent scale corresponds roughly to 0.02 to 0.03 dependency-score units on these scales, and several accepted effects are far above that. For MDM2, H140 was independently validated, and accepted strata H147 and H149 suggest the CDKN2A association is not narrowly limited to TP53-wildtype or MTAP-intact cells. The registered CDKN2A by MTAP interaction among TP53-wildtype cells asks whether the signed CDKN2A effect is larger when MTAP is co-lost, attenuated, or unchanged; alternatives are a broad 9p21 deletion effect, a CDKN2A-specific effect, or no meaningful effect modification. For SMARCA2, H5 is validated; the SMARCA4 by ARID1A interaction tests whether co-loss of another SWI/SNF subunit modifies the synthetic-lethal-like association. For NFE2L2 and STAT3, H20 and H17 are validated; TP53 interactions test whether p53-pathway loss formally modifies the KEAP1 or PTEN effects rather than merely co-occurring with them. For USP7, H73 is validated; the TP53 by MYC-amplification interaction asks whether the TP53 effect differs between MYC-amplified and MYC-intact cells. For WRN, H7 is validated; MSI-high dependency among BRCA2-intact cells tests whether the MSI effect survives after excluding BRCA2-loss cells, although the overlap between MSI-high and BRCA2-loss cells should be monitored. For POLR2A and RPL11, MYC amplification alone was not accepted, so MYC-expression interactions test whether expression-competent MYC amplification creates clinically meaningful dependency only when accompanied by high MYC expression. All proposed comparisons remain observational hypotheses in this dataset; effect modification, specificity, and robustness are not causal claims or external generalizability.

record.narrative: No discovery assessments are due. I request 12 currently untested analyses that test context dependence, technical robustness, and specificity of the strongest accepted associations while avoiding known sparse cells. H154 and H155 ask whether the MDM2-CDKN2A association is formally modified by TP53 status or by MTAP co-loss within TP53-wildtype cells, distinguishing a broad 9p21 co-deletion pattern from a context-specific CDKN2A association. H156 tests whether ARID1A co-loss modifies SMARCA2 dependency in the SMARCA4-loss context. H157 and H158 test whether TP53 loss formally modifies the KEAP1/NFE2L2 and PTEN/STAT3 associations rather than merely co-occurring with them. H159 tests whether MYC amplification modifies the USP7-TP53 association, while H100 through H102 test whether library choice or Cas9 activity formally modifies USP7 and STAT3 associations, complementing the accepted robustness and non-Avana validation results. H160 checks whether the WRN MSI-high association remains after excluding BRCA2-loss cells, assessing possible co-driver confounding. H161 and H162 test MYC-expression-dependent MYC-amplification effects for POLR2A and RPL11, addressing whether MYC-amplified associations require expression-competent MYC rather than genomic amplification alone. These analyses are exploratory and in the supplied dataset only; significant interactions or robustness strata would indicate context-specific associations, not causal mechanism or external generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered direction and negative values oppose it. I used approximate 10 percent outcome-scale thresholds: about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.026 for POLR2A, and 0.025 for RPL11. For MDM2, H154 was very small in the opposite direction and the interval was symmetric around null, so it provides no clinically meaningful TP53 effect modification; H155 supported a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction with a point above threshold but the wide interval included null and both clinically meaningful directions, so it is not decisive. Both are left unresolved and closed as low-information specificity probes. H156 tests whether ARID1A co-loss modifies the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; its signed effect is below the SMARCA2 threshold and imprecise, so there is not enough evidence for a meaningful modification. H157 for NFE2L2/KEAP1 by TP53 loss is small relative to the main KEAP1 effect and imprecise, so it is also unresolved. For STAT3, H158 rejects the registered direction: the signed interval upper bound is below the clinical threshold and the point estimate is opposite the hypothesis. The raw sign suggests attenuation of the PTEN-STAT3 association in TP53-loss cells, but that is a data-driven reversal after multiple interaction tests; I did not accept it, and I registered a separate reversed interaction proposal as a follow-up candidate only. For USP7, H159 has a large point estimate but an interval that includes null and spans both directions, so it is closed as underpowered; H100 and H101 are formal technical-context interactions but are extremely imprecise because the complement cells are small, so they remain unresolved and closed. H160 is a strong positive specificity result: among BRCA2-intact cells, MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency, with a lower bound far above threshold. This supports the robustness and co-driver specificity of the validated MSI-high WRN association. For MYC-expression interactions, H161 rejects the registered POLR2A hypothesis because the signed estimate is opposite and the upper bound is below threshold; H162 for RPL11 has a point just below threshold and a wide interval spanning null, so it is unresolved. The only new result warranting independent validation is H102, the STAT3 PTEN-by-library interaction: it has a lower bound above threshold, but it rests on a small non-Avana complement and conflicts with the already validated non-Avana PTEN effect from H58. I therefore leave H102 active and request validation before accepting any library-context effect modification. These remain observational findings in the supplied dataset; none establishes causality or external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency, now validated and not explained by BRCA2 loss, Cas9, serum, growth, or screen-quality differences. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with independent validation and many consistent strata. record.narrative: This exploration extends the independently validated dataset-only associations into lineage, technical, co-deletion, and biologically motivated context strata rather than adding weak marginal probes. For MDM2, H140 is validated and several strata support a CDKN2A-loss association, especially in TP53-wildtype cells, but the main untested high-value contexts are non-Avana library screens, lineage subgroups, and whether the association survives when MTAP is co-lost. The MDM2 CDKN2A-loss versus intact comparison within TP53-wildtype adenocarcinoma and squamous lines tests whether the effect is general across the two available lung histologic categories. The TP53-wildtype non-Avana test is the most important technical-robustness complement to the accepted Avana stratum. The TP53-wildtype MTAP-loss stratum tests whether the CDKN2A effect is specific to MTAP-intact cells or more broadly reflects a 9p21 co-deletion phenotype. For STAT3, H17 is validated overall and H121 supports a positive PTEN effect in TP53-loss cells; H163 is the data-driven reversed PTEN-by-TP53 interaction and remains active. I therefore register the direct PTEN effect among TP53-wildtype cells as a simpler and more interpretable complement to H163. If the PTEN effect is strong in TP53-wildtype cells, that would be consistent with a broad PTEN-loss association and would make any interaction attenuation less consequential. If it is weak or imprecise while the TP53-loss stratum is accepted, that would be more consistent with possible p53-dependent modification. For NFE2L2, H20 is validated and H68 supports the KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-loss cells; I register the STK11-intact stratum to test whether the KEAP1 association is independent of STK11 loss or whether STK11 co-occurrence is important. Expected signed estimates are positive for all proposed hypotheses, with a stronger expected MDM2/STAT3 effect and a strong expected NFE2L2 effect if the associations generalize within this dataset. Approximate 10 percent thresholds are about 0.027 MDM2 units, 0.028 STAT3 units, and 0.009 NFE2L2 units, so accepted effects far exceed these benchmarks and lower confidence bounds above threshold would support robustness within the supplied dataset. Wide intervals including null or both directions would remain unresolved, especially for sparse lineage or library strata. I keep H163 as the preferred validation candidate because it tests a potentially meaningful modest attenuation of the PTEN-STAT3 association in TP53-loss cells; the new direct TP53-wildtype comparison will help interpret the result if validation is available. All proposed comparisons are observational dataset-only hypotheses, not causal claims or claims of external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

The MDM2 CDKN2A-loss versus intact comparison within TP53-wildtype adenocarcinoma and squamous lines tests whether the effect is general across the two available lung histologic categories. The TP53-wildtype non-Avana test is the most important technical-robustness complement to the accepted Avana stratum. The TP53-wildtype MTAP-loss stratum tests whether the CDKN2A effect is specific to MTAP-intact cells or more broadly reflects a 9p21 co-deletion phenotype. For STAT3, H17 is validated overall and H121 supports a positive PTEN effect in TP53-loss cells; H163 is the data-driven reversed PTEN-by-TP53 interaction and remains active. I therefore register the direct PTEN effect among TP53-wildtype cells as a simpler and more interpretable complement to H163. If the PTEN effect is strong in TP53-wildtype cells, that would be consistent with a broad PTEN-loss association and would make any interaction attenuation less consequential. If it is weak or imprecise while the TP53-loss stratum is accepted, that would be more consistent with possible p53-dependent modification. For NFE2L2, H20 is validated and H68 supports the KEAP1-loss effect in STK11-loss cells; I register the STK11-intact stratum to test whether the KEAP1 association is independent of STK11 loss or whether STK11 co-occurrence is important. Expected signed estimates are positive for all proposed hypotheses, with a stronger expected MDM2/STAT3 effect and a strong expected NFE2L2 effect if the associations generalize within this dataset. Approximate 10 percent thresholds are about 0.027 MDM2 units, 0.028 STAT3 units, and 0.009 NFE2L2 units, so accepted effects far exceed these benchmarks and lower confidence bounds above threshold would support robustness within the supplied dataset. Wide intervals including null or both directions would remain unresolved, especially for sparse lineage or library strata. I keep H163 as the preferred validation candidate because it tests a potentially meaningful modest attenuation of the PTEN-STAT3 association in TP53-loss cells; the new direct TP53-wildtype comparison will help interpret the result if validation is available. The other 11 analyses are targeted context checks for the six validated or strongly supported dataset-only associations. H80 tests whether the large SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency effect is preserved in adenocarcinoma cells; squamous strata are lower priority because the earlier lineage-interaction probe for SMARCA2 was not supportive. H82 and H83 test whether the validated MSI-high WRN dependency effect is preserved in adenocarcinoma and squamous subsets. H84 and H85 test whether the validated KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 association is preserved in the two major lineage subtypes. For MDM2, H164 and H165 test CDKN2A-loss effect magnitude within TP53-wildtype adenocarcinoma and squamous cells; H166 tests technical robustness in non-Avana screens; and H167 tests whether the effect persists in MTAP-loss TP53-wildtype cells, which probes whether the association is broader 9p21 co-deletion context versus a more MTAP-intact-specific pattern. H168 directly estimates the PTEN-loss STAT3 effect in TP53-wildtype cells, giving a simpler and more interpretable complement to the data-driven H163 interaction. H169 estimates the KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect in STK11-intact cells, testing whether the strong KEAP1 association is general within this dataset rather than only evident in STK11-loss contexts. I used approximate 10 percent outcome-scale thresholds: about 0.027 for MDM2, 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.018 for USP7, 0.030 for WRN, 0.026 for POLR2A, and 0.025 for RPL11. For MDM2, H154 was very small in the opposite direction and the interval was symmetric around null, so it provides no clinically meaningful TP53 effect modification; H155 supported a CDKN2A-by-MTAP interaction with a point above threshold but the wide interval included null and both clinically meaningful directions, so it is not decisive. Both are left unresolved and closed as low-information specificity probes. H156 tests whether ARID1A co-loss modifies the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association; its signed effect is below the SMARCA2 threshold and imprecise, so there is not enough evidence for a meaningful modification. H157 for NFE2L2/KEAP1 by TP53 loss is small relative to the main KEAP1 effect and imprecise, so it is also unresolved. For STAT3, H158 rejects the registered direction: the signed interval upper bound is below the clinical threshold and the point estimate is opposite the hypothesis. The raw sign suggests attenuation of the PTEN-STAT3 association in TP53-loss cells, but that is a data-driven reversal after multiple interaction tests; I did not accept it, and I registered a separate reversed interaction proposal as a follow-up candidate only. For USP7, H159 has a large point estimate but an interval that includes null and spans both directions, so it is closed as underpowered; H100 and H101 are formal technical-context interactions but are extremely imprecise because the complement cells are small, so they remain unresolved and closed. record.narrative: All newly delivered estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered contrast and negative values oppose it. I used approximate outcome-scale 10% benchmarks from the absolute outcome means: about 0.025 for dependency_RPL11, 0.042 for dependency_SMARCA2, 0.030 for dependency_WRN, 0.009 for dependency_NFE2L2, 0.027 for dependency_MDM2, and 0.028 for dependency_STAT3. H14/R121 is not supportive: the signed MYC-amplification effect on dependency_RPL11 is -0.0125, the 95% interval is -0.0339 to +0.0090, and the upper bound is below the +0.025 clinically meaningful positive threshold. This excludes a clinically meaningful effect in the registered stronger-dependency direction, although it does not prove exact absence of association; I therefore reject H14 and close it. H80/R122 is a very strong adenocarcinoma-stratum confirmation of the accepted SMARCA4-loss/dependency_SMARCA2 association: signed +0.7770, interval +0.7554 to +0.7987, far above the SMARCA2 threshold. H82/R123 and H83/R124 similarly confirm the validated MSI-high/dependency_WRN association in adenocarcinoma and squamous subsets, with signed estimates +0.7838 and +0.8051 and lower bounds well above the WRN threshold; H83 uses a smaller squamous exposed cell but the effect is extremely large and the interval is reasonably precise. H84/R125 and H85/R126 confirm the accepted KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 direction in adenocarcinoma and squamous subsets, with lower bounds +0.7692 and +0.7665, far above the small NFE2L2 threshold. H164/R127 and H165/R128 support CDKN2A-loss/dependency_MDM2 effects in TP53-wildtype adenocarcinoma and squamous cells, signed +0.1026 and +0.1610 with lower bounds +0.0571 and +0.0832, above the MDM2 threshold. H166/R129 supports technical robustness in non-Avana TP53-wildtype screens: signed +0.1298, interval +0.0401 to +0.2195; although sparse, the lower bound exceeds the threshold and complements the accepted Avana stratum. H167/R130 supports a CDKN2A effect in TP53-wildtype MTAP-loss cells, signed +0.1624 with lower bound +0.0701, consistent with a broader 9p21-loss phenotype rather than an exclusively MTAP-intact effect. H168/R131 gives a direct strong PTEN-loss/dependency_STAT3 effect in TP53-wildtype cells, signed +0.2870, interval +0.2273 to +0.3467, supporting a broad PTEN association rather than a pattern confined to TP53-loss. H169/R132 supports the KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 association in STK11-intact cells, signed +0.8012 with lower bound +0.7789. The only unresolved but potentially important follow-up is H163, the data-driven reversed PTEN-by-TP53 interaction for STAT3: its discovery point +0.097 exceeds the STAT3 threshold but its interval crosses null. Because H121 supports PTEN effects in TP53-loss and H168 supports strong effects in TP53-wildtype cells, independent validation of H163 could determine whether the PTEN-STAT3 association is modestly attenuated by TP53 loss or broadly invariant. I therefore request independent validation of H163. These are dataset-only observational associations; subgroup consistencies do not establish causality, effect modification, or external generalizability.

record.narrative: Scientific synthesis at iteration 10. H140 and H58 response deadlines are resolved. H140 validation R106, signed +0.112 with independent lower bound +0.053, independently confirms the CDKN2A-loss versus intact effect on dependency_MDM2 among TP53-wildtype cells. That lower bound is far above the task-relevant 10-percent scale benchmark of about 0.027 for MDM2, so H140 remains accepted and closed. H58 validation R107, signed +0.358 with independent lower bound +0.127, confirms the PTEN-loss versus intact effect on dependency_STAT3 in non-Avana screens, far above the STAT3 benchmark of about 0.028; H58 remains accepted and closed. H163 is the reversed PTEN-by-TP53 interaction claim for STAT3. Validation R133 is signed +0.009 with interval -0.204 to +0.222, so it is near null and very imprecise. Together with discovery R112, which was also wide, and the accepted direct strata showing positive PTEN effects in both TP53-loss and TP53-wildtype cells, this evidence does not establish a reliable clinically meaningful TP53 modification. I leave H163 unresolved because the interval does not exclude moderate effects, but I close it because further sparse interaction probes are unlikely to be decisive. The strongest supported findings are six dataset-only observational associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, with independent validation and broad robustness across library, lineage, co-deletion, and screen-quality strata. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, with independent validation and robustness across lineage, library, Cas9, growth, serum, mutation-burden, and BRCA2 contexts. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, with independent validation and broad robustness across lineage, library, TP53, MYC, STK11, growth, serum, and screen-quality strata. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, with independent validation overall and in both Avana and non-Avana library contexts, and strong direct strata including TP53-loss, TP53-wildtype, EMT, hypoxia, and STK11-loss cells. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, with independent validation and multiple accepted biological strata. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, independently validated in the TP53-wildtype comparison and supported in many technical, lineage, MTAP, growth, and screen-quality strata. Negative or unsupported findings include the main matched-driver hypotheses: EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF or RIT1 dependency, ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MYC amplification with POLR2A/RPL11/USP7 dependency, and NF1 loss with BRAF or RIT1 dependency. Formal effect-modification claims remain generally unresolved or rejected: Avana-by-PTEN, PIK3CA-by-PTEN, TP53-by-PTEN, lineage modification of several accepted effects, and KRAS STK11/TP53 conditional interactions are not accepted. Several remaining unresolved contexts have been closed as sparse, redundant, or low priority to preserve analysis capacity. The most informative next analyses are the retained direct robustness and lineage strata for accepted effects: H81 squamous SMARCA2, H37/H38 SMARCA2 high-Cas9/high-aneuploidy, H60/H61/H65 STAT3 lineage and IFN contexts, and H75/H76/H78/H79 USP7 library and lineage contexts. These analyses test whether the accepted associations generalize across the main technical and histologic strata present in the supplied dataset. All conclusions remain observational associations in this dataset, not causal claims or statements of external generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

record.narrative: I registered new, falsifiable follow-ups focused on three themes: (1) new biologically motivated main predictors for outcomes where related pathways are already implicated, (2) low-growth robustness of the strongest validated dataset-only associations, and (3) a small number of pathway and technical strata that test whether accepted effects are context-dependent. STK11/LKB1 loss and ARID1A loss are plausible activators of stress/inflammatory signaling, including STAT3-associated programs; for these two hypotheses, direction -1 means stronger dependency is expected in the loss group, so a positive signed estimate would support the claim. RB1 loss is also plausible for stronger WRN dependency because RB1 loss can drive E2F-dependent replication stress; WRN resolves replication stress, so direction -1 again tests stronger dependency with loss. The low-growth comparisons split at 0.6 doublings per day and complement accepted high-growth strata for SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, CDKN2A-MDM2 in TP53-wildtype cells, PTEN-STAT3, and TP53-USP7. These are not intended as new causal claims; they ask whether the magnitude remains clinically meaningful in slower-growing cells. For NFE2L2 and USP7 the accepted directions are weaker dependency (positive raw difference), so direction +1 is registered. PTEN loss within PIK3CA-mutant cells tests whether PTEN-STAT3 dependency remains strong when the PI3K pathway is activated by an alternative driver. Low-Cas9 strata for SMARCA2 and MDM2 provide technical robustness checks alongside accepted high-Cas9/Avana results, though intervals may be wider. Approximate 10-percent benchmarks are about 0.028 STAT3 units, 0.030 WRN units, 0.042 SMARCA2 units, 0.009 NFE2L2 units, 0.027 MDM2 units, and 0.018 USP7 units; signed estimates with lower confidence bounds above these values would support robust associations within this dataset. All proposals remain observational dataset-only associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

The point estimate is below the clinically meaningful threshold and the interval crosses both null and the threshold; this does not support a robust STK11-STAT3 association, but it also does not exclude a modest effect. I mark H170 unresolved and close it because further probing of this particular main-effect screen is low priority. H171/R135, ARID1A loss for dependency_STAT3, gives signed -0.0133 with interval -0.0393 to +0.0128. This opposes the registered stronger-dependency direction and the upper bound is below the +0.028 threshold, so a clinically meaningful effect in that registered direction is excluded for the claim as specified; I reject and close H171. H172/R136, RB1 loss for dependency_WRN, gives signed +0.0154 with interval -0.0216 to +0.0525. The point estimate is below the WRN threshold and the interval crosses null and threshold, leaving the evidence insufficient; H172 is unresolved and closed. The remaining twelve-growth and technical-stratum results are strong confirmations of already supported dataset-only associations rather than new independent causal claims. H173/R137, H174/R138, H175/R139, H176/R140, H177/R141, and H178/R142 test low growth-rate contexts for SMARCA4-SMARCA2, MSI-WRN, KEAP1-NFE2L2, TP53-wildtype CDKN2A-MDM2, PTEN-STAT3, and TP53-USP7. All have lower confidence bounds far above their respective 10% benchmarks, so each is accepted and closed as a robustness stratum. H179/R143 tests PTEN loss within PIK3CA-mutant cells for STAT3 dependency and gives signed +0.268 with lower bound +0.127, well above threshold. The effect is biologically and statistically supportive, but the exposed PTEN-loss cell in PIK3CA-mutant samples is small (38 cells), so I accept it as a cautious dataset-only stratum and close it. H180/R144 and H181/R145 test low-Cas9 technical strata for SMARCA4-SMARCA2 and TP53-wildtype CDKN2A-MDM2. Both have large lower bounds above thresholds and are accepted and closed. Overall, this batch supports persistence of the six validated dataset-only associations across slower-growing and lower-Cas9 contexts, while the new main-effect screens for STK11-STAT3 and RB1-WRN remain inconclusive and ARID1A-STAT3 in the registered direction is not supported. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: Iteration 11 synthesis and scientific report. The only new validation response is H102, the Avana-library interaction for PTEN loss on dependency_STAT3. Discovery R119 supported the registered direction, signed estimate +0.196 with a 95% interval from +0.033 to +0.358, but independent validation R120 is signed -0.064 with a wide interval from -0.292 to +0.164. The validation interval crosses null and the approximate 10-percent STAT3 outcome-scale benchmark, and the point estimate opposes the registered Avana-specific interaction. Because the direct strata show strong PTEN-loss effects in both Avana and non-Avana contexts, and the interaction interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful positive modification, I leave H102 unresolved but closed: the Avana-specific effect-modification claim is not supported, and further sparse probing is unlikely to be decisive. I also close H103 as a low-priority, sparse EGFR-by-KRAS lineage interaction after the main EGFR claim was not accepted. The strongest supported findings are six dataset-only observational associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, independently validated and robust across library, lineage, co-deletion, growth, serum, ploidy, screen-quality, and Cas9 strata. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, independently validated and robust across lineage, library, Cas9, growth, serum, mutation-burden, BRCA2, and screen-quality strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, independently validated and robust across lineage, library, TP53, MYC, STK11, growth, serum, arid1a, screen-quality, and TP53-wildtype or TP53-loss contexts. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, independently validated overall and in non-Avana screens, with accepted strata in Avana screens, both lineages pending confirmation, high-Cas9, low-growth, PIK3CA-mutant, PIK3CA-wildtype, TP53-loss, TP53-wildtype, EMT, hypoxia, STK11-loss, and growth contexts. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, independently validated, with accepted strata including high-Cas9, low-growth, MYC-amplified, CDKN2A-loss, and KEAP1-loss contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells, independently validated and robust across library, lineage, MTAP, growth, serum, screen-quality, and Cas9 strata. Negative or unsupported findings include the main matched-driver hypotheses: EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF or RIT1 dependency, ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MYC amplification with POLR2A or RPL11 dependency, and NF1 loss with BRAF or RIT1 dependency. MYC amplification is also not supported as a main USP7 predictor. Formal effect modification is generally not supported: Avana-by-PTEN STAT3, PIK3CA-by-PTEN STAT3, TP53-by-PTEN STAT3, lineage modification of several accepted effects, EGFR amplification by lineage, ERBB2 amplification by lineage, SMARCA4-by-ARID1A, SMARCA4-by-lineage, KRAS conditional interactions, USP7-by-Cas9, and USP7-by-MYC interactions are rejected, unresolved, or closed. The most informative next analyses are the retained direct lineage and technical strata for accepted associations, especially H37 and H38 for SMARCA2 high-Cas9 and high-aneuploidy contexts, H60 and H61 for PTEN-STAT3 lineage, H65 for STAT3 IFN-high context, H75, H76, H78, and H79 for USP7 library and lineage contexts, H81 for SMARCA2 squamous cells, and H90 for EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant cells. I additionally register H182 to test whether the very strong SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association persists among TP53-loss cells, a biologically relevant co-mutation context. All claims remain observational associations in this supplied dataset, not causal claims or statements of external generalizability. The main unresolved uncertainty is whether the accepted associations remain equally large in the remaining lineage and technical strata, and whether H90 represents a real KRAS-mutant EGFR context or a chance subgroup signal.
