Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments were due at this explore stage. I registered 12 new comparisons designed to test two broad classes of scientifically motivated hypotheses: (1) whether replication-stress or chromatin/epigenetic co-contexts produce dependency relationships beyond the currently supported dataset-only associations, and (2) whether baseline lineage effects are relevant for interpreting accepted associations. The new SMARCA2 claim tests SMARCA4 loss within ARID1A-loss cells, complementing the accepted ARID1A-wildtype stratum and asking whether the strong SMARCA2 dependency remains when two SWI/SNF-associated losses co-occur. The WRN and DHX9 claims test MYC amplification, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and RB1 loss as replication-stress-associated exposures; direction -1 encodes stronger dependency, i.e. more negative raw scores. The KRAS claim tests STK11 loss as a cooperative context for KRAS dependency, while the MDM2 claim tests PTEN loss among TP53-intact cells for a possible PI3K/AKT-MDM2 axis. The STAT3 MYC-amplification claim is a more exploratory but plausible inflammatory/proliferative axis hypothesis. The three direct lineage_subtype claims establish baseline adenocarcinoma-versus-squamous differences for ERBB2, NFE2L2, and STAT3, which is useful because prior accepted effects are often evaluated within lineage strata. I deferred several lower-priority untested technical or lineage strata for accepted associations to make room for these new discovery contrasts; the deferrals are investigation-only changes and do not alter their unresolved status. These proposals remain observational associations in this supplied dataset only and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All newly returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered contrast and negative values oppose it. For these mostly negative dependency scores, I used approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean outcome-scale benchmarks: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, DHX9 about 0.025, KRAS about 0.024, MDM2 about 0.027, STAT3 about 0.028, ERBB2 about 0.026. H182 and H183 test SMARCA4 loss within TP53-loss and ARID1A-loss cells, respectively. Both are huge and precise: R146 has signed estimate +0.773, 95% interval +0.729 to +0.817, and R147 has signed estimate +0.814, interval +0.767 to +0.862. These are far above the SMARCA2 benchmark and support the already robust SMARCA4-SMARCA2 association within biologically relevant co-mutation strata. I accept both as dataset-only observational strata and close them. H184, H185, H186, H187, H189, H190, and H191 test several new main-effect or conditional predictor hypotheses. None supports its registered positive-signed direction at the clinically meaningful scale. H184 is the most interesting exception: MYC amplification gives signed estimate -0.033 with interval -0.064 to -0.002, statistically excluding the registered stronger-WRN-dependency direction and indicating a possible opposite direction, i.e., raw MYC-amplified cells are less negative for WRN dependency. The corresponding reversed-direction interval still crosses the 10% benchmark, so I reject H184 but register a reversal claim only as unresolved rather than accept it. H186 has a similar pattern: RB1 loss gives signed estimate -0.035, interval -0.061 to -0.009, excluding the registered stronger-DHX9-dependency direction but suggesting a possible weaker dependency; I reject the registered claim and register the reversal as unresolved. H185, H187, H189, H190, and H191 have registered-direction upper bounds below their outcome-scale thresholds, so clinically meaningful support for the registered effects is excluded under the current evidence, though some intervals leave modest uncertainty about opposite directions. H188 and H192 remain unresolved: H188 for KEAP1 loss versus WRN dependency has upper interval +0.037, crossing the WRN threshold, and H192 for adenocarcinoma versus squamous ERBB2 dependency has upper interval +0.027, borderline crossing the ERBB2 threshold. H194 is rejected because the adenocarcinoma versus squamous STAT3 contrast has upper bound +0.009, far below the STAT3 threshold. I close the new main-effect screens to avoid over-interpreting multiple exploratory contrasts. I activated H60, H61, H75, H76, H78, and H79 because they address remaining lineage and library strata for already accepted PTEN-STAT3 and TP53-USP7 associations. No independent validation can be requested because the remaining voluntary validation budget is zero. All conclusions remain observational associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

Iteration 12/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: H163 is the reversal interaction claim for the PTEN-by-TP53-loss effect modification on dependency_STAT3. The estimates are already signed to the reversal direction, so positive values support the proposed opposite-direction interaction. Independent validation R133 is signed estimate +0.009, interval -0.204 to +0.222; discovery R112 is signed estimate +0.097, interval -0.024 to +0.217. Relative to the approximate 0.028 practical outcome-scale benchmark for STAT3, the validation point estimate is tiny, and both intervals cross null while still allowing large positive or negative effects. Thus R133 does not support a scientifically meaningful TP53-loss-specific reversal of the PTEN-loss STAT3 effect, but it also does not precisely refute such an effect modification. I therefore leave H163 unresolved and close the investigation; this leaves the registered negative-direction interaction H158 rejected and does not change the accepted PTEN-STAT3 main association. No voluntary validation budget remains, so the main next analyses should use remaining discovery capacity to complete direct lineage and technical strata for already supported associations rather than chase weak multiple-comparison interactions. The supported dataset-only observational findings remain: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency; and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. These associations are robust across many lineage, library, quality, growth, serum, co-mutation, and screen-characteristic strata in this supplied dataset. Matched-driver dependency claims such as EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, and ARID1A loss with SMARCA2 dependency are not supported, as are many effect-modification hypotheses. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in a few conditional or opposite-direction probes, including H90 in KRAS-mutant EGFR context and low-priority reversal observations from WRN/DHX9 screens, plus untested direct strata for accepted effects. The most informative next comparisons are H60/H61 for direct adenocarcinoma and squamous PTEN-STAT3 strata, H78/H79 for direct TP53-USP7 lineage strata, H75/H76 for USP7 library strata, H37/H38 for SMARCA2 under high Cas9 activity and high aneuploidy, H65 for STAT3 in IFN-high contexts, H90 for EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant cells, and baseline lineage contrasts such as H193. All conclusions remain dataset-only observational associations and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this explore stage. I registered 12 new comparisons to use the remaining discovery budget productively. The main strategic priority is not to chase sparse or weak interaction claims, because independent validation is exhausted and many interaction contrasts have been unresolved or rejected. Instead, these proposals test whether the strongest dataset-only observational associations persist in important demographic and biological strata, and whether two additional mechanistically motivated main effects exist outside the already supported predictor-outcome pairs. For the accepted association pattern, direction is retained: direction -1 is used when the hypothesized exposed group has stronger dependency, meaning raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency is more negative; direction +1 is used when the hypothesized exposed group has weaker dependency, meaning raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency is less positive or less negative. Returned estimates will already be signed to the registered direction, so positive values support the registered hypothesis and negative values oppose it. Sex-specific strata for SMARCA2-SMARCA4, WRN-MSI-high, STAT3-PTEN loss, USP7-TP53 loss, MDM2-CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells, and NFE2L2-KEAP1 loss test whether these large effects are robust when evaluated in female cells, not only as artifacts of the male-dominant population or previously tested male strata. The high-stemness PTEN-STAT3 stratum tests whether the PTEN-loss effect remains in a de-differentiated state, which is biologically relevant but could otherwise be confounded by cellular-state heterogeneity. The TP53-loss USP7 stratum within PTEN-loss cells tests whether the TP53-USP7 association persists when a second major tumor-suppressor pathway is altered; a near-null or opposite result would suggest co-pathway buffering or confounding, while a large positive signed estimate would support persistence. The MYC-amplified, TP53-intact MDM2 stratum tests whether the CDKN2A-loss-MDM2 association remains in a proliferative/transcriptionally amplified context. The two new PTEN-loss main-effect claims for POLR2A and RPL11 test a different mechanistic axis: PTEN loss may increase PI3K/AKT/mTOR-associated biosynthetic demand, potentially strengthening dependency on RNA polymerase II and ribosome-biogenesis machinery. The POLR2A MYC-amplification test in low baseline MYC-expression cells tests whether MYC amplification has context-dependent transcriptional effects when baseline MYC mRNA is low; if MYC amplification is buffered or nonfunctional in this setting, the estimate should be near null or opposite. For outcome-scale importance, I will judge signed lower confidence bounds against approximately 10% of the absolute mean dependency score: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, STAT3 about 0.028, MDM2 about 0.027, POLR2A about 0.025, RPL11 about 0.025, and lower but still relevant scales for USP7 and NFE2L2. Because no voluntary validation budget remains, newly discovered effects must be judged from discovery uncertainty, cell sizes, consistency with existing accepted effects, and plausibility, with extra caution for new exploratory axes. All conclusions remain observational associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal effects or claims about generalizability.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due at this analyze stage, so this response is used to request 12 previously untested active claims. The main goal is to complete high-value robustness strata for the strongest accepted dataset-only associations rather than chase sparse interaction claims, because independent validation is exhausted and most interaction contrasts have been unresolved or rejected. H37 and H38 test the very large SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency within high-Cas9 and high-aneuploidy contexts. These address whether the association remains robust when screen quality and genomic complexity differ; given the prior effect magnitude, persistence is likely, but failure would indicate technical or contextual modification. H60 and H61 provide direct adenocarcinoma and squamous strata for the accepted PTEN-loss association with stronger STAT3 dependency, and H78 and H79 do the same for the accepted TP53-loss association with weaker USP7 dependency. H75 and H79 together with H75/H76 test whether the TP53-USP7 effect is driven by a particular CRISPR library; H75 tests Avana-only cells and H76 tests non-Avana cells. H65 tests the PTEN-STAT3 association in high IFN-gamma signature cells, a cellular-state stratum that could reveal immune-signature-dependent modification or robustness. H193 completes a direct lineage baseline for NFE2L2 dependency, which complements the accepted KEAP1-loss effect in both adenocarcinoma and squamous strata. Finally, H205 and H206 test two mechanistically motivated new main effects: PTEN loss on POLR2A and RPL11 dependency, motivated by PI3K-AKT-mTOR-associated transcriptional and ribosome-biogenesis demand. For all requested contrasts, returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the registered direction. I will interpret positive signed effects as supporting the registered hypothesis. For these continuous dependency scores, I will compare signed lower bounds to approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean outcome-scale benchmarks, about 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.028 for STAT3, 0.025 for POLR2A and RPL11, and smaller but still relevant benchmarks for USP7 and NFE2L2, while also weighing uncertainty, cell counts, and consistency with prior accepted effects. All conclusions remain observational associations in the supplied dataset, not causal effects or claims about external generalizability.

H206 tests PTEN loss on RPL11 dependency; the signed interval excludes a clinically meaningful positive registered effect and the point is opposite, so I reject and close it. The new validation budget is zero, so no independent validation request is possible. These conclusions remain dataset-only observational associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

record.narrative:
No assessments were due, and no new validation was delivered; the validation budget is exhausted. Overall, the supplied dataset supports a small number of large, clinically meaningful observational associations between measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores. These associations are robust across many lineage, library, screen-quality, growth, serum, aneuploidy, mutation-burden, and co-alteration strata. By contrast, most matched-driver, lineage-baseline, MYC-biosynthetic, and effect-modification hypotheses are unsupported or remain too uncertain. All conclusions are observational associations in this supplied dataset; they are not causal effects and should not be interpreted as externally generalizable without replication.

Supported findings, with practical relevance judged against approximately 10% of the absolute mean dependency score:
1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger dependency_SMARCA2. Discovery signed estimate +0.784, CI +0.765 to +0.803; validation signed estimate +0.786, CI +0.757 to +0.815. In raw dependency units, SMARCA4-loss cells have SMARCA2 scores about 0.79 units more negative than SMARCA4-intact cells, far above the approximate 0.042 SMARCA2 benchmark.
2. MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger dependency_WRN. Discovery +0.790, CI +0.760 to +0.819; validation +0.805, CI +0.758 to +0.851. This corresponds to WRN scores about 0.80 units more negative in MSI-high cells, far above the approximate 0.030 WRN benchmark.
3. KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker dependency_NFE2L2. Discovery +0.796, CI +0.776 to +0.816; validation +0.829, CI +0.800 to +0.857. Raw scores are about 0.83 units less negative in KEAP1-loss cells, indicating much weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The NFE2L2 mean is near zero, but the absolute effect is very large and precisely estimated.
4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger dependency_STAT3. Discovery +0.267, CI +0.215 to +0.319; validation +0.307, CI +0.228 to +0.387. Raw scores are about 0.31 units more negative in PTEN-loss cells, roughly 95 to 110% of the absolute mean STAT3 scale and well above the approximate 0.028 benchmark.
5. TP53 loss is associated with weaker dependency_USP7. Discovery +0.396, CI +0.325 to +0.467; validation +0.382, CI +0.280 to +0.485. Raw scores are about 0.38 units less negative in TP53-loss cells, far above the approximate 0.018 USP7 benchmark.
6. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger dependency_MDM2. Discovery +0.119, CI +0.079 to +0.158; validation +0.112, CI +0.053 to +0.171. Raw scores are about 0.11 units more negative, about 40 to 50% of the absolute mean MDM2 scale and above the approximate 0.027 benchmark. Additional stratum support is strong, although the central accepted claim is conditional on TP53-intact status.

These supported effects are not merely isolated main contrasts. SMARCA4 loss maintains a very large SMARCA2 effect in Avana and non-Avana libraries, high and lower Cas9 activity, high aneuploidy, high mutation burden, adenocarcinoma, ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, TP53-loss cells, and growth-rate strata. MSI-high maintains a very large WRN effect across lineage subtypes, library, Cas9, serum, growth, screen quality, and BRCA2-loss status. KEAP1 loss maintains a very large NFE2L2 effect across lineage, library, serum, growth, screen quality, STK11, TP53, MYC, and ARID1A strata. PTEN loss maintains a strong STAT3 effect across lineage, library, Cas9, TP53, STK11, PIK3CA, growth, hypoxia, EMT, and IFN-gamma strata. TP53 loss maintains a strong USP7 effect across lineage, library, Cas9, MYC, CDKN2A, KEAP1, and growth strata. CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact cells is consistent across lineage, library, Cas9, growth, screen quality, MTAP, and other co-alteration strata.

Negative or unsupported findings include the following:
- Matched-driver dependency is not supported for most canonical genotype-outcome pairs tested: BRAF V600E did not show meaningful stronger BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification did not show a clinically meaningful main EGFR effect, ERBB2 amplification did not show a meaningful ERBB2 effect, and KRAS mutation did not show a consistent KRAS effect. ARID1A loss did not show the hypothesized SMARCA2 association.
- MYC amplification was not associated with meaningful POLR2A, RPL11, USP7, STAT3, or DHX9 effects. Its associations with KIF18A and WRN were weak or borderline; the WRN reversal signal is small in lower bound and closed as low-priority unresolved.
- TP53 loss was not meaningfully associated with MDM2 dependency overall, although the separate conditional CDKN2A-loss effect among TP53-intact cells was strongly supported.
- New PTEN-loss mechanistic probes were weak: PTEN loss was not associated with meaningful POLR2A or RPL11 dependency.
- Lineage subtype alone was not a robust predictor for the tested dependencies. Adenocarcinoma-versus-squamous contrasts for ERBB2, NFE2L2, STAT3, SMARCA2, and WRN were small, null, or inconsistent.
- Most interaction hypotheses are unsupported. There is no robust evidence for effect modification by lineage, library, Cas9, many co-mutations, IFN/hypoxia/EMT, TP53, MYC, or research markers. The PTEN-by-library STAT3 interaction showed a discovery signal but an opposite near-null validation signal and remains unresolved. The PTEN-by-TP53 interaction remains unsupported in the registered direction and unresolved for the reversal claim.
- Research markers D, E, and F remain untested in the available evidence for dependency_TMED10, so no conclusion can be drawn.

Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in low-precision subgroup and effect-modification claims rather than in the main accepted effects:
- The most informative unresolved discovery is H90: EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant cells has a signed estimate +0.053, CI +0.0035 to +0.103. The point estimate exceeds the approximate 0.025 EGFR benchmark, but the lower confidence bound is below that benchmark and there is no independent validation. Therefore it is scientifically interesting but not accepted.
- MYC amplification versus weaker WRN and RB1 loss versus weaker DHX9 produce small opposite-direction signals with lower bounds below practical thresholds; these are closed as low-priority unresolved observations.
- KRAS effects within STK11-loss contexts and TP53-intact STK11-loss contexts remain unresolved and imprecise.
- Some robustness strata for accepted effects remain untested, including female-specific strata for the main accepted associations and a direct squamous SMARCA4-loss stratum. These do not weaken current conclusions but would improve population-specific robustness assessment.

The most informative next analysis is targeted follow-up of the EGFR amplification effect among KRAS-mutant cells. If independent validation were available, H90 would be the best candidate. Since validation budget is exhausted, the next discovery analyses should test whether this signal survives in high-quality technical subsets, particularly KRAS-mutant cells with high Cas9 activity or Avana screening, and should complete the registered female-stratum tests for the accepted main effects. These targeted analyses are more informative than further broad exploration of already-supported associations or additional sparse interaction hypotheses.

The final scientific conclusion is that this dataset provides strong internal evidence for six association patterns: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, TP53-loss/USP7, and CDKN2A-loss-without-TP53-loss/MDM2. These are large, precisely estimated, validation-supported associations. The evidence does not support the broader hypothesis that matched driver alterations generally predict their own CRISPR dependency in this dataset, nor does it support most effect-modification hypotheses. The EGFR-amplified KRAS-mutant subgroup remains the principal unresolved lead.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains

record.narrative: No assessments are due. With the independent validation budget exhausted, I prioritize high-yield discovery refinements rather than broad low-precision effect modification. The main unresolved discovery lead is H90: EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant cells has a signed estimate of about +0.053 relative to the registered negative dependency direction, but the discovery interval only partly clears the approximate 0.025 EGFR practical benchmark. I therefore register two high-quality technical refinements: KRAS-mutant cells screened with Avana and high Cas9 activity, and KRAS-mutant cells with high screen ROC quality. These are not new biological hypotheses but robustness checks against assay noise; if either gives a signed lower bound above the EGFR benchmark with adequate cell counts, the signal becomes more credible, although it would still be discovery evidence only. I also register low-serum strata for the six accepted main associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, TP53-loss/USP7, and CDKN2A-loss-in-TP53-intact/MDM2. High-serum robustness is already partly supported, but low-serum is mechanistically important because nutrient and culture context can alter dependency. I activate the direct squamous SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 stratum H81 because this accepted effect lacks a clean squamous direct estimate, and activate H153 because the adenocarcinoma subset of the EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant lead is informative despite prior imprecision. I close or defer lower-priority probes with weak prior evidence or redundant mechanistic axes: H111 MYC/KIF18A is near null, H207 POLR2A/MYC low expression is low priority after MYC biosynthetic effects were weak, and H200, H202, H204 are context probes less essential than completing female, low-serum, and direct-lineage robustness. Research markers D, E, and F remain closed for TMED10 because they are constructed assays without assigned biology and the available discovery budget is better spent on accepted-effects robustness and the EGFR/KRAS lead. All new comparisons retain the accepted direction: for stronger dependency hypotheses, direction -1 expects raw exposed-minus-comparator scores to be more negative; for weaker dependency hypotheses, direction +1 expects raw scores to be less negative. Returned estimates and intervals are already signed, so positive signed values support the registered hypothesis. For interpretation, I will use approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean outcome benchmarks and require consistent direction, adequate cell counts, and interval support before accepting a new stratum as a meaningful dataset-only association.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

expectation

With the independent validation budget exhausted, I prioritize high-yield discovery refinements rather than broad low-precision effect modification. The main unresolved discovery lead is H90: EGFR amplification among KRAS-mutant cells has a signed estimate of about +0.053 relative to the registered negative dependency direction, but the discovery interval only partly clears the approximate 0.025 EGFR practical benchmark. I therefore register two high-quality technical refinements: KRAS-mutant cells screened with Avana and high Cas9 activity, and KRAS-mutant cells with high screen ROC quality. These are not new biological hypotheses but robustness checks against assay noise; if either gives a signed lower bound above the EGFR benchmark with adequate cell counts, the signal becomes more credible, although it would still be discovery evidence only. I also register low-serum strata for the six accepted main associations: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, TP53-loss/USP7, and CDKN2A-loss-in-TP53-intact/MDM2. High-serum robustness is already partly supported, but low-serum is mechanistically important because nutrient and culture context can alter dependency. I activate the direct squamous SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 stratum H81 because this accepted effect lacks a clean squamous direct estimate, and activate H153 because the adenocarcinoma subset of the EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant lead is informative despite prior imprecision. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered claim. For practical importance I again used approximate 10% of the absolute mean dependency-score scale as a benchmark: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR about 0.025, and NFE2L2 about 0.009. H81 shows that the SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency remains very large and precise in the squamous stratum: signed estimate +0.805, interval +0.762 to +0.848. This is far above the SMARCA2 benchmark and completes lineage robustness for that accepted association, so I accept and close H81. H197, H198, H199, H201, H203, and H208 provide female-stratum estimates for the six core accepted associations. All have large positive signed estimates with lower bounds far above their outcome benchmarks: SMARCA2 +0.792/+0.756, WRN +0.797/+0.744, STAT3 +0.237/+0.156, USP7 +0.421/+0.313, MDM2 +0.133/+0.068, and NFE2L2 +0.779/+0.746. These are not new biological mechanisms but robustness checks; they support the conclusion that the main dataset-only associations are not confined to male samples or a single demographic stratum. I accept and close all six. H218 tests the moderate CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells in the low-serum context; signed estimate +0.123 with lower bound +0.056 exceeds the MDM2 benchmark, so I accept and close it as a robustness stratum for the accepted conditional association. The EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant lead is less informative. The high-Cas9 subset H209 gives +0.022 but interval -0.046 to +0.091. The Avana subset H210 gives +0.047 but lower bound only -0.007. Avana plus high Cas9 H211 gives +0.027 with lower bound -0.047. The high screen-ROC subset H212 gives the largest point estimate, +0.092, but the lower bound is only +0.008 and the exposed cell has n=20, so it remains below the practical EGFR benchmark and is vulnerable to selection from multiple technical subsets. These checks do not resolve the lead; they show that the signal is not consistently precise enough for acceptance. I leave H209-H212 unresolved and close them. I also close H90 and H153 as unresolved because validation budget is exhausted and the registered technical refinements were not supportive enough. To avoid further fishing in fragile subsets, I propose a single focused effect-modification comparison: whether the EGFR-amplification effect on dependency_EGFR differs between KRAS-mutant and KRAS-intact cells. This tests contingency of the EGFR signal on KRAS context directly, rather than relying on the small KRAS-mutant/EGFR-amplified subset alone. All conclusions remain observational associations in this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

Therefore it is scientifically interesting but not accepted.\n- MYC amplification versus weaker WRN and RB1 loss versus weaker DHX9 produce small opposite-direction signals with lower bounds below practical thresholds; these are closed as low-priority unresolved observations.\n- KRAS effects within STK11-loss contexts and TP53-intact STK11-loss contexts remain unresolved and imprecise.\n- Some robustness strata for accepted effects remain untested, including female-specific strata for the main accepted associations and a direct squamous SMARCA4-loss stratum. If independent validation were available, H90 would be the best candidate. Since validation budget is exhausted, the next discovery analyses should test whether this signal survives in high-quality technical subsets, particularly KRAS-mutant cells with high Cas9 activity or Avana screening, and should complete the registered female-stratum tests for the accepted main effects. These targeted analyses are more informative than further broad exploration of already-supported associations or additional sparse interaction hypotheses.\n\nThe final scientific conclusion is that this dataset provides strong internal evidence for six association patterns: SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2, MSI-high/WRN, KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2, PTEN-loss/STAT3, TP53-loss/USP7, and CDKN2A-loss-without-TP53-loss/MDM2. The evidence does not support the broader hypothesis that matched driver alterations generally predict their own CRISPR dependency in this dataset, nor does it support most effect-modification hypotheses. record.narrative: No new validation was delivered and no claims are due for assessment; the validation budget is exhausted, so the accepted claim set remains unchanged. I reassessed H19, H55, and H56 as active only to allow the already registered but previously untested TMED10 research-marker comparisons to enter future discovery analysis; their scientific status remains unresolved because no evidence has yet been obtained. This synthesis distinguishes supported dataset-only associations, negative findings, unresolved low-precision leads, and the most informative next analyses. All interpretations are observational associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability. For practical relevance, I continued to judge signed effect sizes against approximately 10 percent of the absolute mean dependency-score scale for each outcome, with larger validated intervals required for acceptance. The strongest evidence supports six large, clinically meaningful, internally validated observational associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The core claim H5 has discovery signed estimate +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803 and validation +0.786 with interval +0.757 to +0.815; in raw dependency units, SMARCA4-loss cells are about 0.79 units more negative, far above the SMARCA2 practical benchmark. This effect is robust across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high and lower Cas9 activity, growth strata, high mutation burden, high aneuploidy, adenocarcinoma and squamous strata, ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, TP53-loss cells, male and female strata, and many lineage and quality checks. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency. H7 discovery is +0.790 and validation +0.805, with validation interval +0.758 to +0.851, far above the WRN benchmark. This robustly persists across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, screen quality, BRCA2-loss status, female status, and many other strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The registered reversal H20 has discovery +0.796 and validation +0.829, with validation interval +0.800 to +0.857, meaning raw NFE2L2 scores are much less negative in KEAP1-loss cells. The effect is extremely stable across lineage, library, serum, growth, screen quality, STK11, TP53, MYC, ARID1A, female, and TP53-intact or TP53-loss contexts. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17 discovery +0.267 and validation +0.307 are both large relative to the STAT3 benchmark, and stratum evidence remains strong across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, serum, sex, TP53 status, STK11, PIK3CA, hypoxia, EMT, IFN-gamma, and IFN-gamma-positive contexts. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73 discovery +0.396 and validation +0.382 are far above the USP7 benchmark, with robust strata across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, MYC, CDKN2A, KEAP1, growth, female status, and many co-alteration contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140 discovery +0.119 and validation +0.112 exceed the MDM2 benchmark, with extensive support across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth, screen quality, MTAP, female status, low serum, and co-alteration strata. These six associations are not merely isolated main contrasts; they are the most robust and scientifically meaningful predictor-dependency patterns in the dataset. By contrast, most matched-driver and effect-modification hypotheses are unsupported or unresolved. These are not new biological hypotheses but robustness checks against assay noise; if either gives a signed lower bound above the EGFR benchmark with adequate cell counts, the signal becomes more credible, although it would still be discovery evidence only. H81 shows that the SMARCA4-loss association with stronger SMARCA2 dependency remains very large and precise in the squamous stratum: signed estimate +0.805, interval +0.762 to +0.848. This is far above the SMARCA2 benchmark and completes lineage robustness for that accepted association, so I accept and close H81. H197, H198, H199, H201, H203, and H208 provide female-stratum estimates for the six core accepted associations. All have large positive signed estimates with lower bounds far above their outcome benchmarks: SMARCA2 +0.792/+0.756, WRN +0.797/+0.744, STAT3 +0.237/+0.156, USP7 +0.421/+0.313, MDM2 +0.133/+0.068, and NFE2L2 +0.779/+0.746. These are not new biological mechanisms but robustness checks; they support the conclusion that the main dataset-only associations are not confined to male samples or a single demographic stratum. I accept and close all six. H218 tests the moderate CDKN2A-loss effect on MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells in the low-serum context; signed estimate +0.123 with lower bound +0.056 exceeds the MDM2 benchmark, so I accept and close it as a robustness stratum for the accepted conditional association. The EGFR-amplification/KRAS-mutant lead is less informative. The high-Cas9 subset H209 gives +0.022 but interval -0.046 to +0.091. The Avana subset H210 gives +0.047 but lower bound only -0.007. Avana plus high Cas9 H211 gives +0.027 with lower bound -0.047. The high screen-ROC subset H212 gives the largest point estimate, +0.092, but the lower bound is only +0.008 and the exposed cell has n=20, so it remains below the practical EGFR benchmark and is vulnerable to selection from multiple technical subsets.
