The new proposals test focused, falsifiable hypotheses rather than broad fishing. First, residual matched-driver effects may be masked by genetically incompatible contexts: KRAS-mutant versus KRAS-intact cells among TP53-intact cells may reveal clearer KRAS dependency if TP53 loss dilutes KRAS-specific dependence; BRAF V600E versus wild-type BRAF among KRAS-wild-type cells may reveal driver-specific BRAF dependency if KRAS-mutant samples dilute the effect; ERBB2 amplification versus wild-type ERBB2 among EGFR-intact cells may reveal ERBB2-specific dependency if EGFR co-amplification creates redundancy. Second, I add pathway-plausible secondary hypotheses: STK11 loss may increase dependence on RIT1 if STK11-deficient lung-cancer models rely more heavily on RAS pathway activation; BRCA2 loss under high mutational burden may expose replication-stress dependence on DHX9; TP53 loss under high proliferation may reduce KIF18A dependency because p53-deficient cells tolerate chromosome-missegregation consequences more readily; CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells may alter RPL11 and USP7 dependency through the ARF-MDM2-p53 axis, which is directly supported in this dataset by the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 effect; MYC amplification may increase TMED10 dependency if high-growth cells place greater demand on Golgi secretory trafficking. results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: The new discovery evidence completes the planned low-serum robustness family for five of the six core accepted associations and gives decisive but mostly null or imprecise follow-up on the EGFR lead and several focused biological hypotheses. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction; positive values support the claim. I used approximate 10 percent of the absolute mean dependency scale as the practical benchmark: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, NFE2L2 about 0.009, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR about 0.025, ERBB2 about 0.026, BRAF about 0.025, KRAS about 0.025, DHX9 about 0.025. H213 accepts the low-serum stratum of SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.761 with interval +0.730 to +0.791, far above benchmark. H214 accepts the low-serum stratum of MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency: +0.797 with lower bound +0.750, far above benchmark. H215 accepts the low-serum stratum of KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.771 with lower bound +0.738, far above benchmark. H216 accepts the low-serum stratum of PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.239 with lower bound +0.163, much above benchmark. H217 accepts the low-serum stratum of TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency: +0.333 with lower bound +0.218, far above benchmark. Together with the previously accepted low-serum MDM2 claim H218, the core associations remain clinically meaningful in low-serum culture context. These are robustness checks, not new mechanisms, and they further reduce concern that the accepted associations are driven by a serum-condition artifact. The EGFR amplification context analysis remains insufficient for acceptance. H219 tests the global interaction between EGFR amplification and KRAS mutation status on dependency_EGFR; the signed contrast is +0.037, which is nominally above benchmark, but the interval is -0.020 to +0.095 and does not support the registered direction. H220 restricts the same interaction to adenocarcinoma and gives a near-zero signed contrast +0.002 with interval -0.059 to +0.064. Neither interval provides practical lower-bound support, so the EGFR/KRAS contingency lead is closed. I keep both statuses unresolved rather than rejecting, because the upper confidence limits still admit clinically meaningful differences in the registered direction, but no further validation budget remains and further sparse subset fishing would be scientifically uninformative. H221 tests whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger KRAS dependency among TP53-intact cells; the signed estimate +0.017 is below the KRAS practical benchmark and the interval -0.003 to +0.036 does not provide direction support, so it remains unresolved and is closed. H222 tests BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells; the signed estimate is negative, -0.019, and the upper bound +0.013 is below the BRAF benchmark, indicating no clinically meaningful evidence for the registered stronger-dependency claim; this is rejected and closed. H223 tests ERBB2 amplification among EGFR-intact cells; the signed contrast is essentially zero, +0.0006, interval -0.028 to +0.030. Although the upper bound is slightly above the ERBB2 benchmark, the point estimate is negligible and the prior main and context-level ERBB2 claims were already null, so there is no evidence supporting a meaningful ERBB2 amplification effect in EGFR-intact cells; this is rejected and closed. H224 tests BRCA2 loss under high mutation burden for DHX9 dependency; the signed estimate +0.027 is near benchmark but the interval -0.026 to +0.080 is wide and includes the null and opposite directions. This remains unresolved and is closed because validation budget is exhausted and the context sample is modest. H228 tests CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for weaker USP7 dependency; the signed estimate is negative and negligible, -0.003, interval -0.025 to +0.019, showing no meaningful support and slight opposite tendency. The accepted ARF-MDM2-p53 pattern is specifically captured by CDKN2A-loss-associated stronger MDM2 dependency, not by USP7, so H228 is rejected and closed. Multiplicity is relevant: many discovery contrasts have been examined, and nominal 95 percent intervals were not fully adjusted. The accepted low-serum strata are not borderline; their lower bounds are very far above practical benchmarks and they complement independently validated core claims. The unresolved EGFR, KRAS-TP53-intact, and BRCA2-DHX9 findings are low-precision and do not justify acceptance or causal inference. Remaining active claims are the untested focused biological hypotheses H225 STK11 loss and RIT1 dependency, H226 TP53 loss and KIF18A dependency in high growth, H227 CDKN2A loss and RPL11 dependency among TP53-intact cells, and H229 MYC amplification and TMED10 dependency. All conclusions remain dataset-only associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

With the independent validation budget exhausted, the main scientific priorities are the already accepted six dataset-only associations and the two remaining high-yield unresolved areas: low-serum completeness for accepted effects and the EGFR-amplification by KRAS-mutant context lead. I close H19, H55, H56, H200, H202, and H204 as investigation-only closures because these probes are either unassigned constructed markers or lower-priority context checks relative to the active low-serum and EGFR/KRAS analyses. For TMED10, I instead test a measured biological predictor, MYC amplification, because it is more interpretable than arbitrary research markers. The new proposals test focused, falsifiable hypotheses rather than broad fishing. First, residual matched-driver effects may be masked by genetically incompatible contexts: KRAS-mutant versus KRAS-intact cells among TP53-intact cells may reveal clearer KRAS dependency if TP53 loss dilutes KRAS-specific dependence; BRAF V600E versus wild-type BRAF among KRAS-wild-type cells may reveal driver-specific BRAF dependency if KRAS-mutant samples dilute the effect; ERBB2 amplification versus wild-type ERBB2 among EGFR-intact cells may reveal ERBB2-specific dependency if EGFR co-amplification creates redundancy. Second, I add pathway-plausible secondary hypotheses: STK11 loss may increase dependence on RIT1 if STK11-deficient lung-cancer models rely more heavily on RAS pathway activation; BRCA2 loss under high mutational burden may expose replication-stress dependence on DHX9; TP53 loss under high proliferation may reduce KIF18A dependency because p53-deficient cells tolerate chromosome-missegregation consequences more readily; CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells may alter RPL11 and USP7 dependency through the ARF-MDM2-p53 axis, which is directly supported in this dataset by the accepted CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 effect; MYC amplification may increase TMED10 dependency if high-growth cells place greater demand on Golgi secretory trafficking. I also register an adenocarcinoma-restricted EGFR-amplification-by-KRAS interaction as a more homogeneous complement to the global H219 interaction. All retained and new comparisons use the accepted signed convention: for stronger-dependency claims direction is -1 and raw exposed scores should be more negative; for weaker-dependency claims direction is +1 and raw exposed scores should be less negative; returned signed positive values support the registered claim. Acceptance will require valid cell counts, direction consistent with the hypothesis, and a signed lower bound above an approximate 10% absolute-mean practical benchmark for the relevant outcome, not merely a favorable point estimate. These are observational associations in the supplied dataset only, not causal or generalizable claims.","analyze":"No assessments are due, so this analyze stage allocates remaining discovery tests among previously registered active hypotheses with no useful new evidence. These remain dataset-only associations, not causal effects or claims of generalizability.","appraise":"The new discovery evidence completes the planned low-serum robustness family for five of the six core accepted associations and gives decisive but mostly null or imprecise follow-up on the EGFR lead and several focused biological hypotheses. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction; positive values support the claim. I used approximate 10 percent of the absolute mean dependency scale as the practical benchmark: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, NFE2L2 about 0.009, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR about 0.025, ERBB2 about 0.026, BRAF about 0.025, KRAS about 0.025, DHX9 about 0.025. H213 accepts the low-serum stratum of SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.761 with interval +0.730 to +0.791, far above benchmark. H214 accepts the low-serum stratum of MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency: +0.797 with lower bound +0.750, far above benchmark. H215 accepts the low-serum stratum of KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.771 with lower bound +0.738, far above benchmark. H216 accepts the low-serum stratum of PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.239 with lower bound +0.163, much above benchmark. H217 accepts the low-serum stratum of TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency: +0.333 with lower bound +0.218, far above benchmark. Together with the previously accepted low-serum MDM2 claim H218, the core associations remain clinically meaningful in low-serum culture context. These are robustness checks, not new mechanisms, and they further reduce concern that the accepted associations are driven by a serum-condition artifact. The EGFR amplification context analysis remains insufficient for acceptance. H219 tests the global interaction between EGFR amplification and KRAS mutation status on dependency_EGFR; the signed contrast is +0.037, which is nominally above benchmark, but the interval is -0.020 to +0.095 and does not support the registered direction. H220 restricts the same interaction to adenocarcinoma and gives a near-zero signed contrast +0.002 with interval -0.059 to +0.064. Neither interval provides practical lower-bound support, so the EGFR/KRAS contingency lead is closed. I keep both statuses unresolved rather than rejecting, because the upper confidence limits still admit clinically meaningful differences in the registered direction, but no further validation budget remains and further sparse subset fishing would be scientifically uninformative. H221 tests whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger KRAS dependency among TP53-intact cells; the signed estimate +0.017 is below the KRAS practical benchmark and the interval -0.003 to +0.036 does not provide direction support, so it remains unresolved and is closed. H222 tests BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells; the signed estimate is negative, -0.019, and the upper bound +0.013 is below the BRAF benchmark, indicating no clinically meaningful evidence for the registered stronger-dependency claim; this is rejected and closed. H223 tests ERBB2 amplification among EGFR-intact cells; the signed contrast is essentially zero, +0.0006, interval -0.028 to +0.030. Although the upper bound is slightly above the ERBB2 benchmark, the point estimate is negligible and the prior main and context-level ERBB2 claims were already null, so there is no evidence supporting a meaningful ERBB2 amplification effect in EGFR-intact cells; this is rejected and closed. H224 tests BRCA2 loss under high mutation burden for DHX9 dependency; the signed estimate +0.027 is near benchmark but the interval -0.026 to +0.080 is wide and includes the null and opposite directions. This remains unresolved and is closed because validation budget is exhausted and the context sample is modest. H228 tests CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for weaker USP7 dependency; the signed estimate is negative and negligible, -0.003, interval -0.025 to +0.019, showing no meaningful support and slight opposite tendency. The accepted ARF-MDM2-p53 pattern is specifically captured by CDKN2A-loss-associated stronger MDM2 dependency, not by USP7, so H228 is rejected and closed. Multiplicity is relevant: many discovery contrasts have been examined, and nominal 95 percent intervals were not fully adjusted. The accepted low-serum strata are not borderline; their lower bounds are very far above practical benchmarks and they complement independently validated core claims. The unresolved EGFR, KRAS-TP53-intact, and BRCA2-DHX9 findings are low-precision and do not justify acceptance or causal inference. Remaining active claims are the untested focused biological hypotheses H225 STK11 loss and RIT1 dependency, H226 TP53 loss and KIF18A dependency in high growth, H227 CDKN2A loss and RPL11 dependency among TP53-intact cells, and H229 MYC amplification and TMED10 dependency. All conclusions remain dataset-only associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.","synthesize":"No new validation was delivered and no claims are due for assessment; the validation budget is exhausted, so the accepted claim set remains unchanged. I reassessed H19, H55, and H56 as active only to allow the already registered but previously untested TMED10 research-marker comparisons to enter future discovery analysis; their scientific status remains unresolved because no evidence has yet been obtained. This synthesis distinguishes supported dataset-only associations, negative findings, unresolved low-precision leads, and the most informative next analyses. All interpretations are observational associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or external generalizability. For practical relevance, I continued to judge signed effect sizes against approximately 10 percent of the absolute mean dependency-score scale for each outcome, with larger validated intervals required for acceptance. The strongest evidence supports six large, clinically meaningful, internally validated observational associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency. The core claim H5 has discovery signed estimate +0.784 with interval +0.765 to +0.803 and validation +0.786 with interval +0.757 to +0.815; in raw dependency units, SMARCA4-loss cells are about 0.79 units more negative, far above the SMARCA2 practical benchmark. This effect is robust across Avana and non-Avana libraries, high and lower Cas9 activity, growth strata, high mutation burden, high aneuploidy, adenocarcinoma and squamous strata, ARID1A-loss and ARID1A-intact cells, TP53-loss cells, male and female strata, and many lineage and quality checks. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency. H7 discovery is +0.790 and validation +0.805, with validation interval +0.758 to +0.851, far above the WRN benchmark. This robustly persists across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, screen quality, BRCA2-loss status, female status, and many other strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The registered reversal H20 has discovery +0.796 and validation +0.829, with validation interval +0.800 to +0.857, meaning raw NFE2L2 scores are much less negative in KEAP1-loss cells. The effect is extremely stable across lineage, library, serum, growth, screen quality, STK11, TP53, MYC, ARID1A, female, and TP53-intact or TP53-loss contexts. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17 discovery +0.267 and validation +0.307 are both large relative to the STAT3 benchmark, and stratum evidence remains strong across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, serum, sex, TP53 status, STK11, PIK3CA, hypoxia, EMT, IFN-gamma, and IFN-gamma-positive contexts. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73 discovery +0.396 and validation +0.382 are far above the USP7 benchmark, with robust strata across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, MYC, CDKN2A, KEAP1, growth, female status, and many co-alteration contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140 discovery +0.119 and validation +0.112 exceed the MDM2 benchmark, with extensive support across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth, screen quality, MTAP, female status, low serum, and co-alteration strata. These six associations are not merely isolated main contrasts; they are the most robust and scientifically meaningful predictor-dependency patterns in the dataset. By contrast, most matched-driver and effect-modification hypotheses are unsupported or unresolved. H1 rejects meaningful BRAF V600E effect on BRAF dependency, H3 rejects a meaningful ERBB2 amplification effect on ERBB2 dependency, and H4 leaves the main KRAS mutation effect unresolved with only a small imprecise point estimate. H2 rejects a clinically meaningful main EGFR amplification effect, and H90 leaves the EGFR-amplified KRAS-mutant subgroup as the principal unresolved lead. H6 rejects ARID1A loss as a predictor of stronger SMARCA2 dependency, while the ARID1A interaction H156 is unsupported. MYC amplification was not meaningfully associated with POLR2A, RPL11, USP7 main-effect, STAT3, or DHX9; H184 and H186 reject WRN and DHX9 hypotheses in the registered stronger-dependency direction, while H195 and H196 remain unresolved small opposite-direction observations. TP53 loss was not meaningfully associated with MDM2 overall, but the separate conditional CDKN2A-loss effect among TP53-intact cells is strongly supported. Most interactions and effect modifications are unsupported: lineage-by-driver contrasts, library or Cas9 interactions for accepted effects except unresolved STAT3 library and TP53 interactions, PTEN-by-library H102, PTEN-by-TP53 H158/H163, MYC-by-expression H161/H162, and other co-mutation contexts do not give stable interval support. Lineage subtype alone was generally not a meaningful predictor for tested dependencies where evaluated. Research markers D, E, and F and research signatures have no assigned biology; they are not a priority for mechanistic interpretation. The most informative unresolved scientific question is whether the apparent EGFR amplification signal depends on KRAS-mutant context. H90 has signed estimate +0.053 but lower bound +0.0035 below the EGFR practical benchmark; technical subsets H209-H212 do not resolve it, and validation budget is exhausted. I reassessed the two still-active EGFR-KRAS context claims, H219 and H220, to close investigation without changing their unresolved status. H220/R182 gives a signed EGFR-amplification-by-KRAS-mutation interaction of +0.037 with lower bound -0.020, and H219/R183 gives a KRAS-mutant adenocarcinoma-restricted EGFR-amplification contrast of +0.002 with lower bound -0.059; neither lower bound clears the roughly 0.025 practical benchmark for dependency_EGFR, and the intervals include null and opposite directions. With no validation budget remaining, the EGFR-KRAS contingency lead is closed as unresolved rather than accepted. The supported scientific conclusion from this supplied dataset is a set of six large, internally validated, dataset-only associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency (H5: R5 discovery +0.784, R40 validation +0.786), with lower bounds far above the SMARCA2 benchmark and robust across library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, mutation burden, aneuploidy, lineage, sex, serum, TP53 and ARID1A contexts. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency (H7: R7 +0.790, R93 validation +0.805), robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, screen quality, BRCA2-loss status, and other strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency (H20: R8 +0.796, R79 validation +0.829), meaning raw NFE2L2 scores are substantially less negative in KEAP1-loss cells; this is stable across many co-alteration and technical strata and explains why the original matched-driver direction H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (H17: R24 +0.267, R66 validation +0.307), robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, sex, TP53 status, PIK3CA, STK11, hypoxia, EMT, and IFN-gamma contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency (H140: R88 +0.119, R106 validation +0.112), exceeding the MDM2 benchmark and persisting across lineage, library, serum, growth, screen quality, MTAP, female-status, and co-alteration strata. Low-serum robustness checks H213-H218 further confirm these six core effects rather than adding new mechanisms. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

The accepted core dataset-only associations remain SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency. The new proposals are intended to test either new p53-axis dependencies or high-prior co-alteration refinements of accepted effects. First, dependency_RIT1 is tested for an association with STK11 loss within adenocarcinoma, because RIT1 and STK11 biology are most plausible in adenocarcinoma-like models and the all-lineage main effect may be diluted by squamous samples. Second, TP53 loss is tested for weaker RPL11 and weaker KIF18A dependency; this follows the observed TP53-loss pattern of weaker USP7 dependency and the broader ARF-MDM2-p53 stress-sensor biology, where loss of p53 may reduce dependence on p53-reactivation or chromosome-missegregation tolerance nodes. Third, the accepted PTEN-loss effect on stronger STAT3 dependency is refined to KRAS-mutant cells, because PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathway co-activation may converge on STAT3 survival signaling or, alternatively, dilute the broad PTEN-loss effect. Fourth, the accepted TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss effects are tested in STK11-deficient and KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts, respectively, as falsification checks for whether accepted core effects persist when a strong co-driver is present. Fifth, a reversal-context hypothesis is registered for DHX9: RB1 loss may show stronger dependency under high proliferation if replication stress and transcription-conflict resolution become limiting, despite the main RB1-loss result favoring weaker dependency in R150. Sixth, MYC amplification is tested for stronger TMED10 dependency in high-growth cells, because secretory-trafficking demand may be high-growth dependent even if the global MYC effect is weak. The accepted core dataset-only associations remain SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency. The new proposals are intended to test either new p53-axis dependencies or high-prior co-alteration refinements of accepted effects. First, dependency_RIT1 is tested for an association with STK11 loss within adenocarcinoma, because RIT1 and STK11 biology are most plausible in adenocarcinoma-like models and the all-lineage main effect may be diluted by squamous samples. Second, TP53 loss is tested for weaker RPL11 and weaker KIF18A dependency; this follows the observed TP53-loss pattern of weaker USP7 dependency and the broader ARF-MDM2-p53 stress-sensor biology, where loss of p53 may reduce dependence on p53-reactivation or chromosome-missegregation tolerance nodes. Third, the accepted PTEN-loss effect on stronger STAT3 dependency is refined to KRAS-mutant cells, because PI3K/AKT and RAS/MAPK pathway co-activation may converge on STAT3 survival signaling or, alternatively, dilute the broad PTEN-loss effect. Fourth, the accepted TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss effects are tested in STK11-deficient and KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts, respectively, as falsification checks for whether accepted core effects persist when a strong co-driver is present. Fifth, a reversal-context hypothesis is registered for DHX9: RB1 loss may show stronger dependency under high proliferation if replication stress and transcription-conflict resolution become limiting, despite the main RB1-loss result favoring weaker dependency in R150. Sixth, MYC amplification is tested for stronger TMED10 dependency in high-growth cells, because secretory-trafficking demand may be high-growth dependent even if the global MYC effect is weak. All returned estimates will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction; a positive signed estimate supports the claim. For stronger-dependency claims the raw exposed mean should be more negative; for weaker-dependency claims it should be less negative. Acceptance will require valid cells in every comparison cell and a signed lower bound above the approximate 10 percent absolute-mean practical benchmark for the outcome, about 0.025 for RIT1, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, and TMED10, about 0.028 for STAT3, about 0.018 for USP7, and about 0.009 for NFE2L2. These remain dataset-only associations, not causal effects or claims of generalizability.","appraise":"The new discovery evidence completes the planned low-serum robustness family for five of the six core accepted associations and gives decisive but mostly null or imprecise follow-up on the EGFR lead and several focused biological hypotheses. All estimates are already signed to the registered direction; positive values support the claim. I used approximate 10 percent of the absolute mean dependency scale as the practical benchmark: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, NFE2L2 about 0.009, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR about 0.025, ERBB2 about 0.026, BRAF about 0.025, KRAS about 0.025, DHX9 about 0.025. H213 accepts the low-serum stratum of SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency: signed estimate +0.761 with interval +0.730 to +0.791, far above benchmark. H214 accepts the low-serum stratum of MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency: +0.797 with lower bound +0.750, far above benchmark. H215 accepts the low-serum stratum of KEAP1-loss-associated weaker NFE2L2 dependency: +0.771 with lower bound +0.738, far above benchmark. H216 accepts the low-serum stratum of PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency: +0.239 with lower bound +0.163, much above benchmark. H217 accepts the low-serum stratum of TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency: +0.333 with lower bound +0.218, far above benchmark. Together with the previously accepted low-serum MDM2 claim H218, the core associations remain clinically meaningful in low-serum culture context. These are robustness checks, not new mechanisms, and they further reduce concern that the accepted associations are driven by a serum-condition artifact. The EGFR amplification context analysis remains insufficient for acceptance. H219 tests the global interaction between EGFR amplification and KRAS mutation status on dependency_EGFR; the signed contrast is +0.037, which is nominally above benchmark, but the interval is -0.020 to +0.095 and does not support the registered direction. H220 restricts the same interaction to adenocarcinoma and gives a near-zero signed contrast +0.002 with interval -0.059 to +0.064. Neither interval provides practical lower-bound support, so the EGFR/KRAS contingency lead is closed. I keep both statuses unresolved rather than rejecting, because the upper confidence limits still admit clinically meaningful differences in the registered direction, but no further validation budget remains and further sparse subset fishing would be scientifically uninformative. H221 tests whether KRAS mutation is associated with stronger KRAS dependency among TP53-intact cells; the signed estimate +0.017 is below the KRAS practical benchmark and the interval -0.003 to +0.036 does not provide direction support, so it remains unresolved and is closed. H222 tests BRAF V600E among KRAS-wild-type cells; the signed estimate is negative, -0.019, and the upper bound +0.013 is below the BRAF benchmark, indicating no clinically meaningful evidence for the registered stronger-dependency claim; this is rejected and closed. H223 tests ERBB2 amplification among EGFR-intact cells; the signed contrast is essentially zero, +0.0006, interval -0.028 to +0.030. Although the upper bound is slightly above the ERBB2 benchmark, the point estimate is negligible and the prior main and context-level ERBB2 claims were already null, so there is no evidence supporting a meaningful ERBB2 amplification effect in EGFR-intact cells; this is rejected and closed. H224 tests BRCA2 loss under high mutation burden for DHX9 dependency; the signed estimate +0.027 is near benchmark but the interval -0.026 to +0.080 is wide and includes the null and opposite directions. This remains unresolved and is closed because validation budget is exhausted and the context sample is modest. H228 tests CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for weaker USP7 dependency; the signed estimate is negative and negligible, -0.003, interval -0.025 to +0.019, showing no meaningful support and slight opposite tendency. The accepted ARF-MDM2-p53 pattern is specifically captured by CDKN2A-loss-associated stronger MDM2 dependency, not by USP7, so H228 is rejected and closed. Multiplicity is relevant: many discovery contrasts have been examined, and nominal 95 percent intervals were not fully adjusted. The accepted low-serum strata are not borderline; their lower bounds are very far above practical benchmarks and they complement independently validated core claims. The unresolved EGFR, KRAS-TP53-intact, and BRCA2-DHX9 findings are low-precision and do not justify acceptance or causal inference. Remaining active claims are the untested focused biological hypotheses H225 STK11 loss and RIT1 dependency, H226 TP53 loss and KIF18A dependency in high growth, H227 CDKN2A loss and RPL11 dependency among TP53-intact cells, and H229 MYC amplification and TMED10 dependency. The supported scientific conclusion from this supplied dataset is a set of six large, internally validated, dataset-only associations. record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered claim direction, so positive values support the registered hypothesis and negative values oppose it. I used approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean practical benchmarks for acceptance: RIT1 and RPL11 about 0.025, KIF18A about 0.026, TMED10 and DHX9 about 0.025, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, and NFE2L2 about 0.009. Because independent validation budget is exhausted, every conclusion is a dataset-only association unless separately independently validated. The new p53-ARF follow-up is mostly unsupported or opposite. H225/R194 is essentially null for STK11 loss and RIT1 dependency: signed +0.0016 with interval -0.0201 to +0.0233, whose upper bound is below the RIT1 practical benchmark, so reject. H230/R198 in adenocarcinoma is also near zero, +0.0009 with lower -0.0250 and upper +0.0268; the interval barely admits a 10-percent effect but the estimate and prior global null make this a low-precision lead, so keep unresolved and close rather than overinterpret. H231/R199 and H227/R196 do not support TP53-loss or CDKN2A-loss effects on RPL11 dependency: upper bounds are below the RPL11 benchmark and the signed estimates are weak or opposite, so reject. H226/R195 and H232/R200 are opposite to the registered weaker KIF18A claims: signed estimates -0.0410 and -0.0208 with intervals that either end near zero or are negative. These claims are rejected. The raw pattern in both suggests TP53 loss may instead be associated with stronger KIF18A dependency, which is biologically plausible as a chromosome-missegregation or replication-stress response, but this is post hoc; I registered a reversal proposal as new evidence rather than accepting it here. H229/R197 and H237/R205 do not meet the lower-bound acceptance criterion for MYC-amplification-associated stronger TMED10 dependency. R197 gives signed +0.0087 with lower -0.0136 and upper +0.0309, and R205 gives signed -0.0127 with lower -0.0683 and upper +0.0430. These intervals are wide, low prior from multiple null MYC contrasts, and not direction-supported by the lower bounds; close unresolved. H236/R204 opposes the high-growth RB1-loss stronger DHX9 claim: signed -0.0637 with upper -0.0028, indicating no evidence for the registered direction and instead an opposite weak DHX9 tendency; reject. The important positive context results are H233/R201, H234/R202, and H235/R203. H233 tests PTEN loss within KRAS-mutant cells and yields signed +0.2486 with lower +0.1392, far above the STAT3 benchmark and consistent with the already accepted core PTEN-loss effect; accept. H234 tests TP53 loss within STK11-loss cells and yields signed +0.4899 with lower +0.3124, far above the USP7 benchmark and consistent with the accepted TP53-loss weaker USP7 effect; accept. H235 tests KEAP1 loss within KRAS-mutant cells and yields signed +0.8049 with lower +0.7666, far above the NFE2L2 benchmark and consistent with the accepted KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 effect; accept. These are not new mechanisms but internal evidence that the accepted associations persist in high-prior co-alteration contexts. Multiplicity is a concern because many discovery contrasts have been run and 95-percent Welch intervals are not globally adjusted; the accepted context effects are not borderline and have lower bounds many-fold above practical benchmarks, whereas the unresolved leads have wide intervals and negligible point estimates. I also audited the accepted ledger for coding and logical consistency. H183, as registered, compares arid1a_loss exposed versus comparator while eligibility is arid1a_loss eq 1.0, which logically excludes the comparator group. The positive result R147 and the cell sizes instead resemble a SMARCA4-loss contrast among ARID1A-loss cells, and direct ARID1A-loss contrasts are null in H6/R6 and H39/R20. Therefore H183 cannot be accepted as evidence that ARID1A loss itself is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. I downgraded H183 to unresolved/closed and registered a corrected proposal for SMARCA4 loss among ARID1A-loss cells. This does not undermine the core SMARCA4-loss association H5. All accepted effects remain observational associations in the supplied dataset, not causality, therapeutic necessity, or external generalizability.

Iteration 16/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

refinements to the earlier parent claim.

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this analyze step allocates the 12-comparison allowance entirely to the currently active, previously registered discovery claims. The active queue consists of H200 plus the ten claims registered in the latest explore stage, H240 through H249. The selection follows three principles. First, it tests accepted core dependencies in biologically motivated, untested contexts: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency under high EMT; KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency under hypoxia and among PTEN-loss cells; PTEN loss with STAT3 dependency among low IFN-gamma and high stemness cells; TP53 loss with USP7 dependency among high-proliferation cells; MSI-high with WRN dependency among high-aneuploidy cells; and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact, high-mutation-burden cells with MDM2 dependency. These are robustness tests of existing large dataset-only associations rather than new mechanisms. Second, it tests one new mechanistic candidate: SMARCA4 loss may be associated with stronger DHX9 dependency. Third, it tests two receptor tyrosine kinase cross-talk candidates: ERBB2 amplification may weaken EGFR dependency, and EGFR amplification may weaken ERBB2 dependency. All returned values will already be signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive signed estimates support the registered claim and negative signed estimates oppose it. Acceptance will require valid comparison cells with at least 20 observations in every cell, a signed lower 95% Welch bound above the practical 10-percent-of-absolute-mean benchmark, and an interval consistent with the registered direction. Approximate benchmarks are: SMARCA2 about 0.042, DHX9 about 0.025, NFE2L2 about 0.009, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, WRN about 0.030, MDM2 about 0.027, EGFR about 0.025, and ERBB2 about 0.026. Sparse cells, wide intervals, borderline lower bounds, or direction-inconsistent point estimates will be adjudicated as unresolved or unsupported rather than accepted. Because validation is unavailable, any accepted result will be an association in the supplied dataset only, not evidence of causality, therapeutic necessity, or external generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

H238 tests SMARCA4 loss versus no SMARCA4 loss restricted to ARID1A-loss cells; R147 gives a signed estimate +0.8143 with a 95% Welch lower bound +0.7666 and upper bound +0.8620 in valid comparison cells of 76 and 335. For dependency_SMARCA2, the mean absolute score is about 0.415, so the 10% practical benchmark is roughly 0.042. The R147 lower bound is more than tenfold above that threshold and far above the benchmark, so I accept H238 as a dataset-only refinement: the already accepted SMARCA4-loss/stronger SMARCA2-dependency association persists in ARID1A-deficient cells. This does not support an ARID1A-loss main effect; direct ARID1A-loss contrasts remain unsupported or null in H6/R6 and H39/R20. H239 is the post-hoc reversal of the TP53-loss KIF18A contrast. R200 gives a signed estimate +0.0208, lower +0.0012, upper +0.0403, with valid cells 406 and 1594. Although the raw sign favors stronger KIF18A dependency in TP53-loss cells, the estimate is only about 8% of the mean absolute dependency_KIF18A scale of about 0.256, and the lower bound is far below the approximate 0.0256 practical benchmark. It is also a reversal registered after observing the opposite result in H232. I therefore reject/closed H239 as not scientifically meaningful. The main supported dataset-only findings remain six large core associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5 discovery R5 +0.784 and validation R40 +0.786, with robustness across library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, mutation burden, aneuploidy, ploidy, serum, lineage, sex, TP53 loss, ARID1A-intact status, and now ARID1A-loss status in H238. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency: H7 discovery R7 +0.790 and validation R93 +0.805, robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, growth, screen quality, serum, sex, mutation burden, BRCA2-loss status, media serum, and many co-alteration strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H20 discovery R8 +0.796 and validation R79 +0.829; the original matched-driver direction H8 is rejected because KEAP1-loss raw NFE2L2 scores are much less negative, not more negative. This core effect is stable across STK11-loss, MYC, TP53, KRAS, lineage, sex, serum, growth, Cas9, screen quality, and other contexts. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H17 discovery R24 +0.267 and validation R66 +0.307, robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, sex, TP53 loss, PIK3CA mutation, STK11 loss, KRAS mutation, hypoxia, EMT, IFN-gamma signature, and other strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73 discovery R37 +0.396 and validation R39 +0.382, robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, MYC amplification, CDKN2A loss, KEAP1 loss, STK11 loss, female status, and other co-alterations. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H140 discovery R88 +0.119 and validation R106 +0.112, robust across lineage, library, Cas9 activity, serum, growth, screen quality, MTAP-loss status, female status, and many co-alteration checks. The accepted context claims H233, H234, H235, and now H238 are best read as internal robustness checks of the core PTEN/STAT3, TP53/USP7, KEAP1/NFE2L2, and SMARCA4/SMARCA2 associations rather than as wholly new mechanisms. Negative findings are scientifically important for specificity. BRAF V600E and KRAS-mutant/BRAF contexts do not support the registered BRAF-dependency directions (H1/R1 and H222/R190). ERBB2 amplification does not support the registered ERBB2-dependency direction (H3/R3, H223/R191), and lineage-by-ERBB2 interaction is unsupported (H109/R60). Main EGFR amplification does not support the original stronger-dependency direction (H2/R2 and validation R13 are positive signed for the weaker/less-negative direction), while EGFR-KRAS subgroup and interaction leads remain unresolved or unsupported (H219/R182 and H220/R183). ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 effect (H6/R6, H39/R20), and CDKN2A loss does not support stronger USP7 dependency (H228/R193). Most MYC amplification effects are unsupported or opposite for the registered direction: POLR2A H13/R23, RPL11 H14/R121, KIF18A H111/R61, DHX9 H185/R149, USP7 H10/R10, WRN H184/R148, STAT3 H191/R155, TMED10 H229/R197 and H237/R205. Many lineage contrasts, p53/RAS pathway main effects, RB1, BRCA2, STK11, PIK3CA, APC, and interaction claims were rejected or null. Unresolved low-precision leads should not be reported as vulnerabilities. The KRAS mutation main effect and STK11/TP53 KRAS contexts remain uncertain (H4/R4, H48/R22/R26, H96/R50/R53, H221/R189). The KRAS-mutant EGFR-amplification subgroup is uncertain or inconsistent across technical filters (H90/R44, H209-H212). BRCA2 loss on DHX9 and MSI-high on DHX9 remain uncertain (H16/R12, H224/R192, H137/R85). STK11 loss on RIT1 in adenocarcinoma is near null and low precision (H230/R198). The CDKN2A-MDM2 interaction family remains uncertain (H154/R108, H155/R109). The independent validation budget is exhausted, so these are dataset-only associations and are not causal or generalizable claims. I accepted context effects only when the valid comparison cells were adequate and the signed lower bound clearly exceeded the outcome-specific approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean benchmark. H200/R206 supports PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in high-stemness cells: signed estimate +0.260, lower +0.155, well above the STAT3 benchmark. H241/R208 confirms the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association in EMT-high cells: +0.755 with lower +0.711. H242/R209 and H243/R210 confirm the KEAP1-loss/weaker NFE2L2 association in hypoxia-high cells and among PTEN-loss cells, with lower bounds +0.711 and +0.718. H244/R211 supports PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency in low IFN-gamma cells: +0.144, lower +0.041, modest but above benchmark. H245/R212 supports TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency in high-proliferation cells: +0.413, lower +0.272. H246/R213 supports MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency in high-aneuploidy cells: +0.810, lower +0.749, though exposed n=31 is small; the enormous lower bound still supports acceptance in this dataset.
