record.narrative: No new validation was released and there are no response deadlines. The independent validation budget is exhausted, so this synthesis updates only the scientific summary. The strongest supported conclusions are six dataset-only associations: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with markedly weaker NFE2L2 dependency, the opposite of the initially hypothesized stronger-dependency direction; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency; TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency; and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. Each of these has both discovery and independent validation evidence and accepted robustness in many technical, clinical, genomic, and transcriptional contexts. In dependency-score orientation, more negative values mean stronger dependency, and the signed estimates reported by the controller are already aligned to the claim direction. For SMARCA4 loss versus intact SMARCA4, the accepted H5/R5 signed estimate is +0.784 with validation R40 +0.786, far above the approximate 0.042 ten-percent benchmark for SMARCA2. For MSI-high versus MSS, H7/R7 signed estimate +0.790 and validation R93 +0.805 far exceed the approximate 0.030 WRN benchmark. For KEAP1 loss versus intact KEAP1, H20/R8 signed estimate +0.796 and validation R79 +0.829 exceed the approximate 0.036 NFE2L2 benchmark and show raw less negative NFE2L2 scores, whereas H8 in the opposite direction is rejected. For PTEN loss versus intact PTEN, H17/R24 signed estimate +0.267 and validation R66 +0.307 exceed the approximate 0.028 STAT3 benchmark. For TP53 loss versus intact TP53, H73/R37 signed estimate +0.396 and validation R39 +0.382 exceed the approximate 0.040 USP7 benchmark and indicate less negative USP7 scores. For CDKN2A loss versus intact CDKN2A restricted to TP53-intact cells, H140/R88 signed estimate +0.119 and validation R106 +0.112 exceed the approximate 0.027 MDM2 benchmark. The latest accepted context results are best interpreted as robustness checks: H200/R206 PTEN loss in high-stemness cells; H241/R208 SMARCA4 loss in EMT-high cells; H242/R209 and H243/R210 KEAP1 loss in hypoxia-high and PTEN-loss cells; H244/R211 PTEN loss in low IFN-gamma cells; H245/R212 TP53 loss in high-proliferation cells; H246/R213 MSI-high in high-aneuploidy cells; H247/R214 CDKN2A loss in TP53-intact high-mutation-burden cells; and H238/R147 SMARCA4 loss in ARID1A-loss cells. None of these supports a new causal mechanism; they show that the core associations are not confined to one technical or biological subgroup in this dataset. Negative findings are scientifically important because they constrain interpretation. Direct matched-driver hypotheses are not supported: BRAF V600E does not show stronger BRAF dependency in H1/R1 or KRAS-negative BRAF V600E cells in H222/R190; ERBB2 amplification does not show stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 or EGFR-amplification-negative cells in H223/R191; main EGFR-amplification claims do not support a meaningful EGFR effect, H2/R2 and validation R13 being insufficient and inconsistent; and ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 effect in H6/R6 or in SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20. Most MYC amplification tests are null or opposite for the registered direction, including USP7 H10/R10, POLR2A H13/R23, RPL11 H14/R121, KIF18A H111/R61, WRN H184/R148, DHX9 H185/R149, STAT3 H191/R155, and TMED10 H229/R197 and H237/R205. The new SMARCA4-loss DHX9 hypothesis is rejected, H240/R207 signed estimate -0.0055 with upper bound +0.0138 below the DHX9 benchmark. Important unresolved areas remain. KRAS-mutation dependency effects and KRAS-STK11-TP53 co-alteration contexts are low precision or inconsistent, including H4/R4, H48/R22 and R26, H96/R50 and R53, H74/R38, and H221/R189. EGFR amplification in KRAS-mutant subgroups and EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk remain unresolved because intervals are wide and point estimates are small, including H90/R44, H209-R212, H219/R182, H220/R183, H21/R21, H248/R215, and H249/R216. BRCA2 and MSI effects on DHX9 are also not supported as meaningful effects, H16/R12, H224/R192, and H137/R85. Interaction evidence generally does not show reliable modification of the core effects; for example, H102 library interaction is unresolved after discordant validation, H154/R108 and H155/R109 MDM2 interactions are uncertain, and H158/R112 with validation R133 does not support reliable STAT3-TP53 interaction modification. Because no new validation budget remains, no further validation can be requested. The most informative next analysis is independent replication of exactly these six core associations with the same directional hypothesis and a clinically meaningful effect-size criterion. If external validation becomes available, test SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, MSI-high on WRN, KEAP1 loss on NFE2L2 in the weaker-dependency direction, PTEN loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on USP7 in the weaker-dependency direction, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 among TP53-intact cells. If no external replication is possible, stop broad discovery fishing; only high-prior conditional or interaction tests that can plausibly exceed the outcome-specific ten-percent benchmark and have sufficient cell sizes are scientifically worth pursuing. The accepted results should be reported as strong internal associations in this supplied CRISPR dataset, not as causal vulnerabilities or general therapeutic claims.

Iteration 18/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support the registered association. For stronger-dependency claims (direction -1), the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is more negative, meaning stronger CRISPR dependency in the exposed group; for weaker-dependency claims for NFE2L2 and USP7 (direction +1), the raw score is less negative in the exposed group. Every signed lower 95% bound clearly exceeds the outcome-specific approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean practical benchmark. SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 effects are large in hypoxia-high, stemness-high, and prior EMT-high contexts (R217/R227). MSI-high/WRN effects are large in EMT-high, hypoxia-high, and stemness-high contexts (R218/R222/R225). KEAP1-loss/weaker-NFE2L2 effects are large in EMT-high and stemness-high contexts (R220/R224). TP53-loss/weaker-USP7 effects are robust in EMT-high and hypoxia-high contexts (R219/R223). CDKN2A-loss/stronger-MDM2 among TP53-intact cells persists in EMT-high and stemness-high contexts (R221/R226), with lower bounds 0.074 and 0.067 versus the MDM2 benchmark around 0.027. PTEN-loss/stronger-STAT3 also persists among MYC-amplified cells (R228; lower bound 0.174 versus STAT3 benchmark around 0.028). Some exposed cells are small but above the minimum (e.g., WRN n=28-32 and MYC-amplified STAT3 n=49), so the intervals are wide relative to the core population; however, the effect sizes and lower bounds are far above the practical threshold. Multiplicity and post-hoc subgroup selection are concerns, but these tests follow already accepted core associations and the margins are large enough that modest multiplicity inflation would not overturn them. These conclusions remain dataset-only associations and do not establish causality, therapeutic necessity, or external generalizability. No validation is requested because the independent validation budget is exhausted.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

expectation

record.narrative: No assessments are due and no independent validation budget remains, so this explore stage registers focused internal robustness follow-ups rather than new mechanisms or validation. The accepted dataset-only core associations are tested in unmeasured co-alteration contexts that are biologically important in lung adenocarcinoma biology: STK11/LKB1-loss and STK11-intact contexts, TP53-intact contexts, KEAP1-intact context, and MYC co-alteration contexts. These tests address whether the core effects remain scientifically meaningful under plausible co-mutations rather than only under average or previously tested technical strata. For stronger-dependency claims, a more negative dependency score in the exposed group is expected, so direction and anticipated raw exposed-minus-comparator are negative. For weaker-dependency claims involving NFE2L2 and USP7, a less negative score in the exposed group is expected, so direction and anticipated raw contrasts are positive. The signed controller output should be interpreted without re-multiplying by direction. Falsifiable alternatives are no meaningful difference in the registered context, an opposite context-specific effect, or failure because cells are too small or intervals are too wide. Acceptance will require valid Welch comparison cells with at least 20 observations in each cell, a signed lower 95% bound above the outcome-specific approximate 10-percent absolute-mean practical benchmark, and interval support for the registered direction. Approximate benchmarks are SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, USP7 about 0.018, NFE2L2 about 0.009, MDM2 about 0.027, and STAT3 about 0.028. Any accepted result remains a measured association in this supplied dataset and does not establish causality, therapeutic necessity, or external generalizability.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Unresolved uncertainty remains for KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2 and MSI effects on DHX9, and smaller subgroup effect modification. The most informative next analysis is prespecified external replication of exactly these six core associations with the same signed hypothesis and a 10-percent practical effect criterion: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, MSI-high on WRN, KEAP1 loss on weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on weaker USP7, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 among TP53-intact cells. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73/R37 +0.396, validation R39 +0.382, versus benchmark about 0.018. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H140/R88 +0.119, validation R106 +0.112, versus benchmark about 0.027. These core associations remain directionally consistent across many technical and biological contexts, including lineage subgroups, CRISPR library, Cas9 activity, growth rate, media serum, proliferation, aneuploidy, mutation burden, IFN-gamma, EMT, hypoxia, stemness, and several co-alteration contexts, so they are internally robust but still only dataset-only associations. Important negative findings constrain the biological story. Direct matched-driver dependencies are not supported: BRAF V600E does not show meaningful stronger BRAF dependency in H1/R1 or KRAS-negative cells in H222/R190, and ERBB2 amplification does not show meaningful stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 or EGFR-amplification-negative cells in H223/R191. EGFR amplification does not show a stable clinically meaningful main effect, with H2/R2 and validation R13 small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 effect in H6/R6 or SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20. Interaction claims mostly do not show reliable modification of the core effects; library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, and EGFR interaction analyses are usually wide, null, discordant, or below practical thresholds. Unresolved uncertainty remains for KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2 and MSI effects on DHX9, and smaller subgroup effect modification. The most informative next analysis is prespecified external replication of exactly these six core associations with the same signed hypothesis and a 10-percent practical effect criterion: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, MSI-high on WRN, KEAP1 loss on weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on weaker USP7, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 among TP53-intact cells. Unresolved uncertainty remains for KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2 and MSI effects on DHX9, and smaller subgroup effect modification. The most informative next analysis is prespecified external replication of exactly these six core associations with the same signed hypothesis and a 10-percent practical effect criterion: SMARCA4 loss on SMARCA2, MSI-high on WRN, KEAP1 loss on weaker NFE2L2, PTEN loss on STAT3, TP53 loss on weaker USP7, and CDKN2A loss on MDM2 among TP53-intact cells. record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this explore stage registers only focused follow-up comparisons rather than new broad mechanisms. The accepted core dataset-only associations already have large effects and internal validation, but their robustness under high-quality screening, important co-alteration contexts, and culture/locus-specific confounding can still be assessed. For SMARCA2/SMARCA4 loss, USP7/TP53 loss, and STAT3/PTEN loss, I register mean-difference comparisons restricted to observations with screen_roc_auc at or above the median, because these three core associations have not yet been formally tested in this high-screen-discrimination context. For WRN/MSI-high, I register a stricter high-quality stratum using both adequate Cas9 activity and high screen_roc_auc, and also an STK11-loss context because STK11 co-alteration is biologically important in lung cancer and the MSI-high/WRN effect has been shown in STK11-intact but not STK11-loss contexts. The MTAP-loss proposal is a specificity test for the CDKN2A-loss/MDM2 signal: testing MTAP loss only among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells asks whether the 9p21/MDM2 association is driven by CDKN2A loss specifically or by co-deletion of nearby MTAP. MDM2/CDKN2A media-serum-10 and SMARCA2/SMARCA4 media-serum-10 complete selected technical robustness checks. Direction conventions remain unchanged: for stronger-dependency claims involving SMARCA2, WRN, STAT3, and MDM2, direction is -1 and a positive signed estimate means more negative raw dependency scores in the exposed group; for the weaker-dependency USP7/TP53 claim, direction is +1 and a positive signed estimate means less negative raw dependency scores in the exposed group. Controller estimates are already signed and must not be remultiplied. Acceptance will require valid Welch cells with at least 20 observations per cell, interval support in the registered direction, and a signed lower bound above the approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean practical benchmark: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, USP7 about 0.018, STAT3 about 0.028, and MDM2 about 0.027. Null or underpowered results will be interpreted as insufficient evidence for a meaningful association in that specific context, not as proof that the association is absent, causal, or externally generalizable.

Iteration 20/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and no independent validation request can be made because the validation budget is exhausted. The only active, untested registered comparisons are H274-H281, so this analyze stage requests all eight. These are focused robustness and specificity tests rather than new broad fishing. For USP7/NFE2L2 direction +1 claims, positive signed estimates mean less negative raw scores, i.e. weaker dependency. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All eight newly delivered comparisons are valid Welch tests with at least 20 observations in each cell, and the reported estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. H274 shows that SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency persists in the high-screen-quality stratum defined by screen_roc_auc at or above its median: signed estimate 0.791 with signed lower bound 0.764, far above the approximate 10-percent absolute-mean practical benchmark for SMARCA2 of about 0.042. H275 shows that TP53-loss-associated weaker USP7 dependency persists in the same high-screen-quality stratum: signed estimate 0.426 with lower bound 0.332, far above the USP7 benchmark of about 0.018. H276 shows that PTEN-loss-associated stronger STAT3 dependency persists in the high-screen-quality stratum: signed estimate 0.253 with lower bound 0.181, far above the STAT3 benchmark of about 0.028. H277 shows that MSI-high-associated stronger WRN dependency persists even under the combined quality stratum of adequate Cas9 activity and high screen_roc_auc: signed estimate 0.804 with lower bound 0.758, far above the WRN benchmark of about 0.030. H278 tests MSI-high and WRN in STK11-loss cells. The estimate is large, 0.749 with signed lower bound 0.675, also far above the WRN benchmark, so I accept it as a dataset-only association, but I note caution because the exposed STK11-loss/MSI-high cell has only 22 observations, which is barely above the minimum cell-size requirement and makes the stratum fragile to influential points. H279 tests whether MTAP loss alone, among CDKN2A-intact TP53-intact cells, is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. The signed estimate is tiny, 0.0088, and the confidence interval includes zero and has a lower bound of -0.0154, below the MDM2 practical benchmark of about 0.027. This provides no meaningful support for an MTAP-only effect in this stratum, but it is not sufficient evidence to prove absence of MTAP biology; therefore H279 is unresolved and closed. This keeps CDKN2A-specificity plausible without claiming definitive locus-specific causality. H280 shows that CDKN2A-loss-associated stronger MDM2 dependency persists among TP53-intact cells in high-serum media: signed estimate 0.115 with lower bound 0.067, above the MDM2 benchmark. H281 shows that SMARCA4-loss-associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency persists in high-serum media: signed estimate 0.799 with lower bound 0.774, far above the SMARCA2 benchmark. I also close H267 as unresolved because, although the CDKN2A-loss direction in the TP53-intact STK11-loss stratum is positive, its signed lower bound of 0.0174 is below the MDM2 benchmark. Multiplicity remains a concern, but the accepted effects are so far above practical benchmarks that reasonable multiplicity adjustments would not overturn them. H278 and H279 are the least stable new results: H278 because of a small exposed cell and H279 because the interval remains compatible with null and clinically negligible effects. All conclusions remain associations within this supplied lung CRISPR-screen dataset, not causal vulnerabilities or externally generalizable claims. No validation request is made because the independent validation budget is exhausted.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

  "narrative": "No new validation estimates or response deadlines were delivered at this synthesis, and the independent validation budget is exhausted with remaining_new_requests 0. assessments_due is empty, so no status changes are made and the controller-maintained accepted-claim set remains unchanged. This is the final scientific synthesis of the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset.

Supported findings, all interpreted as dataset-only measured associations rather than causal vulnerabilities or externally generalizable claims, are strongest for six signed dependencies. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5/R5 signed estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R40 at 0.786, interval 0.757 to 0.815. The effect is far above the approximate practical benchmark for SMARCA2 and remains in many strata, including library strata, adequate Cas9 activity, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H7/R7 signed estimate 0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, validated by R93 at 0.805, interval 0.758 to 0.851. This is one of the largest and most internally consistent effects in the run, though the STK11-loss WRN stratum H278 is accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, contrary to the initially expected stronger-dependency direction: H20/R8 signed estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R79 at 0.829, interval 0.800 to 0.857, while the opposite-direction claim H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H17/R24 signed estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R66 at 0.307, interval 0.228 to 0.387. This effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the STAT3 practical benchmark and robust across many technical and biological strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73/R37 signed estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R39 at 0.382, interval 0.280 to 0.485. The direction is weaker dependency, and the association is internally stable across library, quality, lineage, growth, serum, and co-alteration contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H140/R88 signed estimate 0.119, interval 0.079 to 0.158, validated by R106 at 0.112, interval 0.053 to 0.171. This is the most biologically interpretable of the smaller effects and remains robust in several technical, lineage, and co-alteration strata, although it is less extreme than the first five associations.

These six findings are not causal claims. They are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores in a lung-cell-line CRISPR-screen dataset. They may reflect genetic, copy-number, transcriptomic, culture, screening-quality, lineage, or co-alteration structure in this dataset. Independent validation strengthens internal consistency but does not establish mechanism, clinical causality, or external generalizability. The accepted core effects are large enough and sufficiently consistent that multiplicity concerns are unlikely to overturn them, but all secondary subgroup and interaction findings remain more exploratory.

Negative or non-supported findings constrain the interpretation. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported: BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or H222/R190; ERBB2 amplification is null for ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and H223/R191; and EGFR amplification is not stable as a direct EGFR-dependency association, with H2/R2 rejected and validation R13 small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or in SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20, which helps distinguish the accepted SMARCA4-loss association from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, and TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS dependency interactions with STK11-loss and TP53-loss contexts do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted subgroups remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful.

Interaction and effect-modification analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the main effects. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2, and STAT3 interaction claims are usually null, discordant, underpowered, or below practical-effect thresholds. For example, H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, and H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. The WRN STK11-loss stratum is directionally accepted but small, and the MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H267/R234 remains unresolved because the signed lower bound is below the MDM2 practical benchmark. MTAP-only specificity testing H279/R246 is unresolved and provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. This keeps CDKN2A-specific interpretation plausible but does not prove locus-specific causality.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts, underpowered subgroup analyses, and several direct driver hypotheses. These include KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only effects, and many lineage or technical subgroup effects that closed as unresolved. Lack of significance in these analyses is not evidence of absence; many intervals are wide or compatible with trivial effects.

record.narrative:
No new validation estimates or response deadlines were delivered at this synthesis, and the independent validation budget is exhausted with remaining_new_requests 0. assessments_due is empty, so no status changes are made and the controller-maintained accepted-claim set remains unchanged. This is the final scientific synthesis of the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset.

Supported findings, all interpreted as dataset-only measured associations rather than causal vulnerabilities or externally generalizable claims, are strongest for six signed dependencies. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5/R5 signed estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R40 at 0.786, interval 0.757 to 0.815. The effect is far above the approximate practical benchmark for SMARCA2 and remains in many strata, including library strata, adequate Cas9 activity, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H7/R7 signed estimate 0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, validated by R93 at 0.805, interval 0.758 to 0.851. This is one of the largest and most internally consistent effects in the run, though the STK11-loss WRN stratum H278 is accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, contrary to the initially expected stronger-dependency direction: H20/R8 signed estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R79 at 0.829, interval 0.800 to 0.857, while the opposite-direction claim H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H17/R24 signed estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R66 at 0.307, interval 0.228 to 0.387. This effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the STAT3 practical benchmark and robust across many technical and biological strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73/R37 signed estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R39 at 0.382, interval 0.280 to 0.485. The direction is weaker dependency, and the association is internally stable across library, quality, lineage, growth, serum, and co-alteration contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H140/R88 signed estimate 0.119, interval 0.079 to 0.158, validated by R106 at 0.112, interval 0.053 to 0.171. This is the most biologically interpretable of the smaller effects and remains robust in several technical, lineage, and co-alteration strata, although it is less extreme than the first five associations.

These six findings are not causal claims. They are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores in a lung-cell-line CRISPR-screen dataset. They may reflect genetic, copy-number, transcriptomic, culture, screening-quality, lineage, or co-alteration structure in this dataset. Independent validation strengthens internal consistency but does not establish mechanism, clinical causality, or external generalizability. The accepted core effects are large enough and sufficiently consistent that multiplicity concerns are unlikely to overturn them, but all secondary subgroup and interaction findings remain more exploratory.

Negative or non-supported findings constrain the interpretation. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported: BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or H222/R190; ERBB2 amplification is null for ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and H223/R191; and EGFR amplification is not stable as a direct EGFR-dependency association, with H2/R2 rejected and validation R13 small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or in SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20, which helps distinguish the accepted SMARCA4-loss association from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, and TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS dependency interactions with STK11-loss and TP53-loss contexts do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted subgroups remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful.

Interaction and effect-modification analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the main effects. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2, and STAT3 interaction claims are usually null, discordant, underpowered, or below practical-effect thresholds. For example, H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, and H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. The WRN STK11-loss stratum is directionally accepted but small, and the MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H267/R234 remains unresolved because the signed lower bound is below the MDM2 practical benchmark. MTAP-only specificity testing H279/R246 is unresolved and provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. This keeps CDKN2A-specific interpretation plausible but does not prove locus-specific causality.

Unresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts, underpowered subgroup analyses, and several direct driver hypotheses. These include KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only effects, and many lineage or technical subgroup effects that closed as unresolved. Lack of significance in these analyses is not evidence of absence; many intervals are wide or compatible with trivial effects.

The most informative next analysis is not further broad internal subgroup fishing in this dataset. It should be a prespecified external replication of exactly the six core signed associations: SMARCA4 loss on stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high on stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss on weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss on stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss on weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss on stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells. The replication protocol should preserve the same exposure and comparator definitions, signed directions, eligibility conditions, practical-effect thresholds, minimum cell-count rules, and screening-quality stratifications. If external replication is unavailable, future internal work should be limited to a small number of high-prior conditional effects with prespecified hypotheses, adequate cell counts, and independent replication, with special care for small-cell strata such as STK11-loss co-alteration contexts.

This effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the STAT3 practical benchmark and robust across many technical and biological strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73/R37 signed estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R39 at 0.382, interval 0.280 to 0.485. The direction is weaker dependency, and the association is internally stable across library, quality, lineage, growth, serum, and co-alteration contexts.
