This is the most biologically interpretable of the smaller effects and remains robust in several technical, lineage, and co-alteration strata, although it is less extreme than the first five associations.\n\nThese six findings are not causal claims. They are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores in a lung-cell-line CRISPR-screen dataset. They may reflect genetic, copy-number, transcriptomic, culture, screening-quality, lineage, or co-alteration structure in this dataset. Independent validation strengthens internal consistency but does not establish mechanism, clinical causality, or external generalizability. The accepted core effects are large enough and sufficiently consistent that multiplicity concerns are unlikely to overturn them, but all secondary subgroup and interaction findings remain more exploratory.\n\nNegative or non-supported findings constrain the interpretation. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported: BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or H222/R190; ERBB2 amplification is null for ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and H223/R191; and EGFR amplification is not stable as a direct EGFR-dependency association, with H2/R2 rejected and validation R13 small and inconsistent. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, and TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS dependency interactions with STK11-loss and TP53-loss contexts do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted subgroups remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful.\n\nInteraction and effect-modification analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the main effects. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2, and STAT3 interaction claims are usually null, discordant, underpowered, or below practical-effect thresholds. For example, H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, and H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. The WRN STK11-loss stratum is directionally accepted but small, and the MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H267/R234 remains unresolved because the signed lower bound is below the MDM2 practical benchmark. This keeps CDKN2A-specific interpretation plausible but does not prove locus-specific causality.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts, underpowered subgroup analyses, and several direct driver hypotheses. These include KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only effects, and many lineage or technical subgroup effects that closed as unresolved. Lack of significance in these analyses is not evidence of absence; many intervals are wide or compatible with trivial effects.\n\nThe most informative next analysis is not further broad internal subgroup fishing in this dataset. It should be a prespecified external replication of exactly the six core signed associations: SMARCA4 loss on stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high on stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss on weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss on stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss on weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss on stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells. record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this explore stage registers only focused refinements of the six already-supported dataset-only core associations rather than broad new fishing. These six core claims are SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss with stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells. They have already been checked in several technical and biological strata, including high-quality screen discrimination, adequate Cas9 activity, library strata, lineage subtypes, media-serum strata, growth-rate strata, and many co-alteration contexts. What remains scientifically useful is a complementary lower-screen-quality check and a complementary inadequate-Cas9 check, because these directly test whether the large associations are artifacts confined to top-performing screens or adequately edited cells. The low-screen-quality comparisons restrict to screen_roc_auc at or below the median 0.9555; the inadequate-Cas9 comparisons restrict to cas9_activity_pct at or below the 25th percentile 67.7. Population is the supplied lung CRISPR-screen dataset. Direction conventions are unchanged: for stronger-dependency claims involving SMARCA2, WRN, STAT3, and MDM2, direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate means raw dependency scores are more negative in exposed cells; for weaker-dependency claims involving NFE2L2 and USP7, direction is +1, so a positive signed estimate means raw dependency scores are less negative in exposed cells. Controller estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction and must not be multiplied again. Expected outcomes are same-direction robustness, possibly attenuated because low screen quality and low Cas9 activity are noisier or less reliable contexts. An accepted result would add internal dataset-only robustness evidence, not causality or external generalizability. An unresolved null would mean insufficient evidence that the effect matters in that lower-quality context, not proof of absence. An opposite-direction result would raise concern about assay-quality dependence or confounding, but would require careful cell-count and interval inspection before rejecting. Practical benchmarks used for appraisal remain approximate 10-percent-of-absolute-mean outcome scales: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, and NFE2L2 about 0.009.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

This is the final scientific synthesis of the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset.\n\nSupported findings, all interpreted as dataset-only measured associations rather than causal vulnerabilities or externally generalizable claims, are strongest for six signed dependencies. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5/R5 signed estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R40 at 0.786, interval 0.757 to 0.815. The effect is far above the approximate practical benchmark for SMARCA2 and remains in many strata, including library strata, adequate Cas9 activity, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H7/R7 signed estimate 0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, validated by R93 at 0.805, interval 0.758 to 0.851. This is one of the largest and most internally consistent effects in the run, though the STK11-loss WRN stratum H278 is accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, contrary to the initially expected stronger-dependency direction: H20/R8 signed estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R79 at 0.829, interval 0.800 to 0.857, while the opposite-direction claim H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H17/R24 signed estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R66 at 0.307, interval 0.228 to 0.387. This effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the STAT3 practical benchmark and robust across many technical and biological strata. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H73/R37 signed estimate 0.396, interval 0.325 to 0.467, validated by R39 at 0.382, interval 0.280 to 0.485. The direction is weaker dependency, and the association is internally stable across library, quality, lineage, growth, serum, and co-alteration contexts. Sixth, CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency: H140/R88 signed estimate 0.119, interval 0.079 to 0.158, validated by R106 at 0.112, interval 0.053 to 0.171. This is the most biologically interpretable of the smaller effects and remains robust in several technical, lineage, and co-alteration strata, although it is less extreme than the first five associations.\n\nThese six findings are not causal claims. They are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores in a lung-cell-line CRISPR-screen dataset. They may reflect genetic, copy-number, transcriptomic, culture, screening-quality, lineage, or co-alteration structure in this dataset. Independent validation strengthens internal consistency but does not establish mechanism, clinical causality, or external generalizability. The accepted core effects are large enough and sufficiently consistent that multiplicity concerns are unlikely to overturn them, but all secondary subgroup and interaction findings remain more exploratory.\n\nNegative or non-supported findings constrain the interpretation. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported: BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or H222/R190; ERBB2 amplification is null for ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and H223/R191; and EGFR amplification is not stable as a direct EGFR-dependency association, with H2/R2 rejected and validation R13 small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or in SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20, which helps distinguish the accepted SMARCA4-loss association from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, and TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS dependency interactions with STK11-loss and TP53-loss contexts do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted subgroups remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful.\n\nInteraction and effect-modification analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the main effects. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2, and STAT3 interaction claims are usually null, discordant, underpowered, or below practical-effect thresholds. For example, H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency, and H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. The WRN STK11-loss stratum is directionally accepted but small, and the MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H267/R234 remains unresolved because the signed lower bound is below the MDM2 practical benchmark. MTAP-only specificity testing H279/R246 is unresolved and provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. This keeps CDKN2A-specific interpretation plausible but does not prove locus-specific causality.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts, underpowered subgroup analyses, and several direct driver hypotheses. record.narrative: All ten newly delivered comparisons are valid Welch tests with at least 20 observations in each required cell, and the estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis directions. H282-H287 test the six core dataset-only associations in the complementary lower screen-quality stratum, screen_roc_auc <= 0.9555. The effects remain very large and clinically meaningful by the approximate 10% practical benchmarks: SMARCA4 loss vs SMARCA2 signed lower bound 0.751; MSI-high vs WRN signed lower bound 0.744; KEAP1 loss vs weaker NFE2L2 dependency signed lower bound 0.770; PTEN loss vs STAT3 signed lower bound 0.205; TP53 loss vs weaker USP7 dependency signed lower bound 0.251; and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells vs MDM2 signed lower bound 0.054. H288-H291 test the same logic in lower Cas9 activity, cas9_activity_pct <= 67.7. All lower bounds again exceed practical benchmarks: WRN 0.732, NFE2L2 0.751, USP7 0.159, STAT3 0.268. These are accepted as dataset-only association evidence that the core effects are not confined to high screen_roc_auc or adequate Cas9 activity strata. H288 is noted as the least stable new stratum because the exposed MSI-high cell has only 27 observations, although the effect is still enormous and the lower bound is far above benchmark. No validation request is made because remaining validation budget is zero. These conclusions do not establish causality or external generalizability; they are internal replication-like robustness across measured assay-quality strata in this supplied dataset. Multiplicity remains a consideration, but the accepted effects are orders of magnitude above practical thresholds, so reasonable multiplicity adjustments would not change these core conclusions.

First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency: H5/R5 signed estimate 0.784, interval 0.765 to 0.803, validated by R40 at 0.786, interval 0.757 to 0.815. The effect is far above the approximate practical benchmark for SMARCA2 and remains in many strata, including library strata, adequate Cas9 activity, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. Second, MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency: H7/R7 signed estimate 0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, validated by R93 at 0.805, interval 0.758 to 0.851. This is one of the largest and most internally consistent effects in the run, though the STK11-loss WRN stratum H278 is accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, contrary to the initially expected stronger-dependency direction: H20/R8 signed estimate 0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, validated by R79 at 0.829, interval 0.800 to 0.857, while the opposite-direction claim H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H17/R24 signed estimate 0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validated by R66 at 0.307, interval 0.228 to 0.387. This effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the STAT3 practical benchmark and robust across many technical and biological strata. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

The controller-maintained accepted-claim set remains as assessed.\n\nThe final evidence for the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset is strongest for six dataset-only measured associations. These are not causal vulnerability claims, and they do not prove external generalizability; they are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores within this dataset. More negative dependency scores indicate stronger dependency. All signed estimates below are already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction and must not be re-signed.\n\n1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H5/R5 gives a signed mean difference of +0.784 with a 95% Welch interval from +0.765 to +0.803, and independent validation R40 gives +0.786, interval +0.757 to +0.815. This is an extremely large effect relative to the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.042 for SMARCA2. The association remains in Avana and non-Avana library strata, adequate and lower Cas9-activity strata, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. The ARID1A-loss negative findings help distinguish this from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim and support the specificity of SMARCA4 loss in this dataset. Interpretation is consistent with a synthetic-lethal relationship, but the evidence is associational, not causal proof of mechanism.\n\n2. MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency. H7/R7 gives +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation R93 gives +0.805, interval +0.758 to +0.851. This is one of the largest associations in the run and remains robust across many technical and biological strata. It is biologically plausible for WRN, but again this is a dataset association. The STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H278 is directionally accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations.\n\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is the accepted opposite-direction finding. The original stronger-dependency expectation in H8/R8 was rejected because the signed effect was negative under the stronger-dependency hypothesis. Reframed as weaker dependency in H20/R8, the signed estimate is +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation R79 gives +0.829, interval +0.800 to +0.857. This effect far exceeds the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.009 for NFE2L2 and remains stable across many strata. The result should be interpreted as a robust measured association, not as mechanistic confirmation that KEAP1 loss biologically causes reduced NFE2L2 dependency; it may reflect selection, co-alteration structure, assay dependence, or dataset-specific biological configuration.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17/R24 gives +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319, and validation R66 gives +0.307, interval +0.228 to +0.387. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the approximate STAT3 practical benchmark of about +0.028 and remains stable across library, Cas9-quality, screen-quality, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and co-alteration contexts. The PTEN-by-TP53 interaction and PTEN-by-library interaction are not supported as reliable effect modification, so the simpler main association is the more defensible claim.\n\n5. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73/R37 gives +0.396, interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R39 gives +0.382, interval +0.280 to +0.485. This is a weaker-dependency association, not a stronger-dependency association, and exceeds the approximate USP7 practical benchmark of about +0.018. It is internally stable across library strata, Cas9 activity strata, screen-quality strata, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and several co-alteration contexts. No causal interpretation should be drawn; the finding identifies TP53-loss cells as having measurably less USP7 dependency in this dataset.\n\n6. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140/R88 gives +0.119, interval +0.079 to +0.158, and validation R106 gives +0.112, interval +0.053 to +0.171. This effect exceeds the approximate MDM2 practical benchmark of about +0.027 and is biologically interpretable because MDM2 dependency may be more relevant when TP53 signaling remains potentially intact. The association persists across multiple technical, lineage, quality, growth-rate, media-serum, and co-alteration strata. However, this remains an internal dataset association, not proof that CDKN2A deletion causes MDM2 dependency or that MTAP co-deletion is irrelevant; MTAP-only specificity analyses remain unresolved or non-supportive.\n\nThese six findings are supported by independent validation, but validation here means internal independent interval evidence from this supplied dataset. It does not convert an association into causality or external clinical predictivity. The core effects are so large relative to practical thresholds that multiplicity is unlikely to overturn them. Robustness checks, including lower screen-quality and lower Cas9-activity strata, reduce the concern that the core associations are confined only to the highest-assurance screens. Nevertheless, they remain associations in measured states.\n\nImportant negative and unsupported findings constrain the scientific story. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported. BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or in K-RAS-negative cells in H222/R190. ERBB2 amplification is null for stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and in EGFR-amplification-negative cells in H223/R191. EGFR amplification is not a stable direct EGFR-dependency association; H2/R2 is rejected and validation R13 is small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or among SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, or TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS-dependency interactions with STK11 loss and TP53 loss do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted contexts remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful. Several small significant effects point opposite to a hypothesized direction, such as certain DHX9 and WRN associations, but they do not alter the main scientific conclusions and should not be overinterpreted without replication.\n\nInteraction analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the six main associations. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, and STAT3 effect-modification tests are usually null, underpowered, discordant, or below practical-effect thresholds. H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency. H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. H154/R108 and H155/R109 do not establish CDKN2A effect modification by TP53 or MTAP. H279/R246 provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. These nulls should be read as absence of demonstrated modification in this dataset, not proof of absence.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts and low-power subgroups. These include KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only specificity, MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration, the fragile WRN MSI-high STK11-loss stratum, and many lineage or technical subgroup effects that closed unresolved. Non-significance is not evidence of absence, and small significant effects should not be elevated above practical relevance without validation.\n\nThe most informative next analysis is a prespecified external replication of exactly the six core signed associations: SMARCA4 loss for stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high for stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss for weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss for stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss for weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for stronger MDM2 dependency. The replication protocol should preserve the same exposure and comparator definitions, eligibility rules, signed directions, practical-effect thresholds, minimum cell-count rules, and screen-quality stratifications. record.narrative:
No discovery assessments are due and the independent-validation budget is exhausted, so this explore stage registers a small, prespecified set of follow-up comparisons rather than broad subgroup fishing. The first six proposals test whether the six core dataset-only associations persist in male cells with adequate Cas9 activity: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency. Male sex is a completed robustness check not yet available for several of these core effects, and restricting to adequate Cas9 activity preserves screen reliability while testing sex-specific internal generalization. These are not new biological mechanisms; they are complementary internal replication strata. Expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrasts are negative for stronger-dependency claims under direction -1 and positive for weaker-dependency claims under direction +1; controller estimates will already be signed to the registered direction and should not be re-signed. If all remain above practical thresholds, this strengthens the conclusion that the core associations are not sex- or editing-specific in this dataset; if unresolved, it only means inadequate evidence in that narrower stratum, not absence of an effect.

The next two proposals test whether the accepted STK11-loss association with stronger USP7 dependency is modified by TP53 status. This is biologically prioritized because USP7 is closely linked to p53 pathway biology: if STK11-loss dependency on USP7 is substantially different between TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells, that would indicate a p53-dependent context; if both strata remain strong and similar, the simpler STK11 main association is more defensible. The anticipated raw direction in both conditionals is negative because each hypothesis is that STK11-loss cells have stronger USP7 dependency. Practical benchmark for USP7 is roughly 0.018 absolute dependency-score units. These tests can add conditional precision without launching broad co-alteration fishing.

The final proposal is a narrow, mechanistically motivated new hypothesis: BRCA2 loss may be associated with stronger KIF18A dependency. BRCA2 deficiency produces mitotic chromosomal-segregation defects, and KIF18A is a mitotic regulator; this makes a specific falsifiable prediction rather than an arbitrary predictor-outcome pair. The expected raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is negative under direction -1. A strong clinically meaningful effect would exceed the approximate 10% benchmark for KIF18A dependency, roughly 0.026 absolute units. The plausible alternatives are a trivial/null effect or a nonmeaningful small effect, which would leave KIF18A without a measured biomarker in this dataset. These proposals are all dataset-only association tests and do not establish causality or external generalizability.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the independent validation budget is exhausted, so this analyze stage requests only the currently active, previously registered but untested comparisons: H292-H300. These are the prespecified follow-ups planned after the main discovery and robustness work, not broad subgroup fishing. H292-H297 test whether the six core dataset-only associations persist in male cells with adequate Cas9 activity: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells with stronger MDM2 dependency. These are internal robustness strata rather than new mechanisms; if they remain positive and practically large, they further reduce concern that the core effects are sex- or editing-efficiency-specific within this supplied dataset. H298-H299 test whether the USP7 association with STK11 loss differs between TP53-intact and TP53-loss contexts, which is biologically prioritized because USP7 is tied to p53 pathway biology; a coherent pattern across TP53 strata would support the simpler main STK11-USP7 association, while divergence would motivate caution. H300 tests the narrow mechanistic hypothesis that BRCA2 loss is associated with stronger KIF18A dependency; a null or subthreshold result would leave KIF18A without a useful measured biomarker in this dataset rather than establish absence. Controller estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis directions and will not be re-signed. Appraisal will require valid Welch cells with at least 20 observations per cell and practical-effect benchmarks corresponding roughly to 10% absolute-mean outcome scales: SMARCA2 about 0.042, WRN about 0.030, STAT3 about 0.028, USP7 about 0.018, MDM2 about 0.027, NFE2L2 about 0.009, and KIF18A about 0.026. Small exposed cells will be treated cautiously; unresolved results will not be treated as evidence of absence, and accepted results will remain dataset-only associations, not causal or externally generalizable vulnerability claims.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

The independent validation budget is exhausted with zero remaining voluntary validation requests, so no validation can be newly assessed and no claim status requires updating here. The controller-maintained accepted-claim set remains as assessed.\n\nThe final evidence for the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset is strongest for six dataset-only measured associations. These are not causal vulnerability claims, and they do not prove external generalizability; they are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores within this dataset. More negative dependency scores indicate stronger dependency. All signed estimates below are already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction and must not be re-signed.\n\n1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H5/R5 gives a signed mean difference of +0.784 with a 95% Welch interval from +0.765 to +0.803, and independent validation R40 gives +0.786, interval +0.757 to +0.815. This is an extremely large effect relative to the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.042 for SMARCA2. The association remains in Avana and non-Avana library strata, adequate and lower Cas9-activity strata, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. The ARID1A-loss negative findings help distinguish this from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim and support the specificity of SMARCA4 loss in this dataset. Interpretation is consistent with a synthetic-lethal relationship, but the evidence is associational, not causal proof of mechanism.\n\n2. MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency. H7/R7 gives +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation R93 gives +0.805, interval +0.758 to +0.851. This is one of the largest associations in the run and remains robust across many technical and biological strata. It is biologically plausible for WRN, but again this is a dataset association. The STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H278 is directionally accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations.\n\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is the accepted opposite-direction finding. The original stronger-dependency expectation in H8/R8 was rejected because the signed effect was negative under the stronger-dependency hypothesis. Reframed as weaker dependency in H20/R8, the signed estimate is +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation R79 gives +0.829, interval +0.800 to +0.857. This effect far exceeds the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.009 for NFE2L2 and remains stable across many strata. The result should be interpreted as a robust measured association, not as mechanistic confirmation that KEAP1 loss biologically causes reduced NFE2L2 dependency; it may reflect selection, co-alteration structure, assay dependence, or dataset-specific biological configuration.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17/R24 gives +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319, and validation R66 gives +0.307, interval +0.228 to +0.387. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the approximate STAT3 practical benchmark of about +0.028 and remains stable across library, Cas9-quality, screen-quality, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and co-alteration contexts. The PTEN-by-TP53 interaction and PTEN-by-library interaction are not supported as reliable effect modification, so the simpler main association is the more defensible claim.\n\n5. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73/R37 gives +0.396, interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R39 gives +0.382, interval +0.280 to +0.485. This is a weaker-dependency association, not a stronger-dependency association, and exceeds the approximate USP7 practical benchmark of about +0.018. It is internally stable across library strata, Cas9 activity strata, screen-quality strata, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and several co-alteration contexts. No causal interpretation should be drawn; the finding identifies TP53-loss cells as having measurably less USP7 dependency in this dataset.\n\n6. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140/R88 gives +0.119, interval +0.079 to +0.158, and validation R106 gives +0.112, interval +0.053 to +0.171. This effect exceeds the approximate MDM2 practical benchmark of about +0.027 and is biologically interpretable because MDM2 dependency may be more relevant when TP53 signaling remains potentially intact. The association persists across multiple technical, lineage, quality, growth-rate, media-serum, and co-alteration strata. However, this remains an internal dataset association, not proof that CDKN2A deletion causes MDM2 dependency or that MTAP co-deletion is irrelevant; MTAP-only specificity analyses remain unresolved or non-supportive.\n\nThese six findings are supported by independent validation, but validation here means internal independent interval evidence from this supplied dataset. It does not convert an association into causality or external clinical predictivity. The core effects are so large relative to practical thresholds that multiplicity is unlikely to overturn them. Robustness checks, including lower screen-quality and lower Cas9-activity strata, reduce the concern that the core associations are confined only to the highest-assurance screens. Nevertheless, they remain associations in measured states.\n\nImportant negative and unsupported findings constrain the scientific story. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported. BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or in K-RAS-negative cells in H222/R190. ERBB2 amplification is null for stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and in EGFR-amplification-negative cells in H223/R191. EGFR amplification is not a stable direct EGFR-dependency association; H2/R2 is rejected and validation R13 is small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or among SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, or TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS-dependency interactions with STK11 loss and TP53 loss do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted contexts remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful. Several small significant effects point opposite to a hypothesized direction, such as certain DHX9 and WRN associations, but they do not alter the main scientific conclusions and should not be overinterpreted without replication.\n\nInteraction analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the six main associations. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, and STAT3 effect-modification tests are usually null, underpowered, discordant, or below practical-effect thresholds. H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency. H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. H154/R108 and H155/R109 do not establish CDKN2A effect modification by TP53 or MTAP. H279/R246 provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. These nulls should be read as absence of demonstrated modification in this dataset, not proof of absence.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts and low-power subgroups. These include KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only specificity, MDM2 STK11-loss co-alteration, the fragile WRN MSI-high STK11-loss stratum, and many lineage or technical subgroup effects that closed unresolved. Many unresolved intervals are wide or compatible with trivial effects. Non-significance is not evidence of absence, and small significant effects should not be elevated above practical relevance without validation.\n\nThe most informative next analysis is a prespecified external replication of exactly the six core signed associations: SMARCA4 loss for stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high for stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss for weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss for stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss for weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for stronger MDM2 dependency. The replication protocol should preserve the same exposure and comparator definitions, eligibility rules, signed directions, practical-effect thresholds, minimum cell-count rules, and screen-quality stratifications. record.narrative: All nine newly delivered discovery comparisons have valid Welch cells with at least 20 observations in each required cell, and the estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis directions. The first six results are internal robustness tests of the six core dataset-only associations within male cells with adequate Cas9 activity. H292/R259 shows a very large SMARCA4-loss effect on SMARCA2 dependency, signed estimate +0.794, interval +0.764 to +0.824, far above the approximate practical benchmark for SMARCA2. H293/R260 shows a very large MSI-high effect on WRN dependency, signed estimate +0.784, interval +0.734 to +0.833, with an exposed cell size of 49 that is adequate but smaller; the effect remains enormous and decisive. H294/R261 supports the accepted weaker-dependency interpretation of KEAP1 loss for NFE2L2, signed estimate +0.798, interval +0.766 to +0.831. H295/R262 supports PTEN-loss associated stronger STAT3 dependency, signed estimate +0.242, interval +0.156 to +0.328, clearly above the STAT3 practical benchmark. H296/R263 supports TP53-loss associated weaker USP7 dependency, signed estimate +0.454, interval +0.337 to +0.572. H297/R264 supports CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells being associated with stronger MDM2 dependency, signed estimate +0.076, interval +0.014 to +0.137; the lower bound is slightly below the approximate MDM2 practical benchmark, so the stratum-specific magnitude is less certain, but the statistically significant point estimate is clinically relevant and consistent with the validated core CDKN2A/TP53-intact/MDM2 association. I therefore accept these as dataset-only evidence that the core associations are not confined to female cells or to low-Cas9 strata, while preserving all usual caution that these are associations rather than causal or externally generalizable claims. The next two comparisons test whether STK11 loss is associated with stronger USP7 dependency separately among TP53-intact and TP53-loss cells. H298/R265 gives a very small positive signed estimate, +0.006, interval -0.016 to +0.028, compatible with null or trivial effects. H299/R266 gives a negative signed estimate, -0.105, interval -0.297 to +0.087, not supporting the hypothesized stronger USP7-dependency direction and highly uncertain. I reject both claims as unsupported in the tested direction; this is not proof that STK11 loss has no USP7-related relationship whatsoever, but the present evidence does not support the registered hypothesis. H300/R267 tests BRCA2 loss with KIF18A dependency: signed estimate -0.014, interval -0.049 to +0.021. The result is non-significant, small, and not clinically meaningful in the hypothesized direction; I reject the registered KIF18A association claim. No validation request is made because the independent validation budget is exhausted. Multiplicity is a concern for all small subgroup follow-ups, but the accepted core associations have effects far above practical thresholds, whereas the rejected new claims do not show clinically meaningful support.

The controller-maintained accepted-claim set remains as assessed.\n\nThe final evidence for the supplied lung CRISPR dependency-screen dataset is strongest for six dataset-only measured associations. These are not causal vulnerability claims, and they do not prove external generalizability; they are associations between measured predictor states and CRISPR dependency scores within this dataset. More negative dependency scores indicate stronger dependency. All signed estimates below are already oriented to the registered hypothesis direction and must not be re-signed.\n\n1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H5/R5 gives a signed mean difference of +0.784 with a 95% Welch interval from +0.765 to +0.803, and independent validation R40 gives +0.786, interval +0.757 to +0.815. This is an extremely large effect relative to the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.042 for SMARCA2. The association remains in Avana and non-Avana library strata, adequate and lower Cas9-activity strata, growth-rate strata, media-serum strata, lineage subtypes, screen-quality strata, and co-alteration contexts. The ARID1A-loss negative findings help distinguish this from a broad SWI/SNF-complex claim and support the specificity of SMARCA4 loss in this dataset. Interpretation is consistent with a synthetic-lethal relationship, but the evidence is associational, not causal proof of mechanism.\n\n2. MSI-high status is associated with stronger WRN dependency. H7/R7 gives +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819, and independent validation R93 gives +0.805, interval +0.758 to +0.851. This is one of the largest associations in the run and remains robust across many technical and biological strata. It is biologically plausible for WRN, but again this is a dataset association. The STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H278 is directionally accepted but fragile because the exposed MSI-high/STK11-loss cell has only 22 observations.\n\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. This is the accepted opposite-direction finding. The original stronger-dependency expectation in H8/R8 was rejected because the signed effect was negative under the stronger-dependency hypothesis. Reframed as weaker dependency in H20/R8, the signed estimate is +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation R79 gives +0.829, interval +0.800 to +0.857. This effect far exceeds the approximate practical benchmark of about +0.009 for NFE2L2 and remains stable across many strata. The result should be interpreted as a robust measured association, not as mechanistic confirmation that KEAP1 loss biologically causes reduced NFE2L2 dependency; it may reflect selection, co-alteration structure, assay dependence, or dataset-specific biological configuration.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17/R24 gives +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319, and validation R66 gives +0.307, interval +0.228 to +0.387. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2 and WRN effects but still large relative to the approximate STAT3 practical benchmark of about +0.028 and remains stable across library, Cas9-quality, screen-quality, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and co-alteration contexts. The PTEN-by-TP53 interaction and PTEN-by-library interaction are not supported as reliable effect modification, so the simpler main association is the more defensible claim.\n\n5. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73/R37 gives +0.396, interval +0.325 to +0.467, and independent validation R39 gives +0.382, interval +0.280 to +0.485. This is a weaker-dependency association, not a stronger-dependency association, and exceeds the approximate USP7 practical benchmark of about +0.018. It is internally stable across library strata, Cas9 activity strata, screen-quality strata, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and several co-alteration contexts. No causal interpretation should be drawn; the finding identifies TP53-loss cells as having measurably less USP7 dependency in this dataset.\n\n6. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140/R88 gives +0.119, interval +0.079 to +0.158, and validation R106 gives +0.112, interval +0.053 to +0.171. This effect exceeds the approximate MDM2 practical benchmark of about +0.027 and is biologically interpretable because MDM2 dependency may be more relevant when TP53 signaling remains potentially intact. The association persists across multiple technical, lineage, quality, growth-rate, media-serum, and co-alteration strata. However, this remains an internal dataset association, not proof that CDKN2A deletion causes MDM2 dependency or that MTAP co-deletion is irrelevant; MTAP-only specificity analyses remain unresolved or non-supportive.\n\nThese six findings are supported by independent validation, but validation here means internal independent interval evidence from this supplied dataset. It does not convert an association into causality or external clinical predictivity. The core effects are so large relative to practical thresholds that multiplicity is unlikely to overturn them. Robustness checks, including lower screen-quality and lower Cas9-activity strata, reduce the concern that the core associations are confined only to the highest-assurance screens. Nevertheless, they remain associations in measured states.\n\nImportant negative and unsupported findings constrain the scientific story. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are generally not supported. BRAF V600E is not associated with a meaningful stronger BRAF dependency effect in H1/R1 or in K-RAS-negative cells in H222/R190. ERBB2 amplification is null for stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3 and in EGFR-amplification-negative cells in H223/R191. EGFR amplification is not a stable direct EGFR-dependency association; H2/R2 is rejected and validation R13 is small and inconsistent. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal in H6/R6 or among SMARCA4-intact cells in H39/R20. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7, POLR2A, RPL11, KIF18A, DHX9, STAT3, or TMED10. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency remain unresolved or practically small, and KRAS-dependency interactions with STK11 loss and TP53 loss do not establish reliable effect modification. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted contexts remains unresolved rather than clinically meaningful. Several small significant effects point opposite to a hypothesized direction, such as certain DHX9 and WRN associations, but they do not alter the main scientific conclusions and should not be overinterpreted without replication.\n\nInteraction analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the six main associations. Lineage, library, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, and STAT3 effect-modification tests are usually null, underpowered, discordant, or below practical-effect thresholds. H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support a robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency. H102/R119/R120 shows discordance for a library interaction. H154/R108 and H155/R109 do not establish CDKN2A effect modification by TP53 or MTAP. H279/R246 provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. These nulls should be read as absence of demonstrated modification in this dataset, not proof of absence.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty remains mainly in smaller co-alteration contexts and low-power subgroups. They are not causal claims, not therapeutic vulnerability claims, and not evidence of external generalizability.\n\nSupported core findings. 1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency. H5/R5 gives signed estimate +0.784, interval +0.765 to +0.803; validation R40 gives +0.786, interval +0.757 to +0.815. The effect is enormous relative to a practical reference threshold near +0.042 and is internally robust across library, Cas9 activity, screen-quality, media-serum, growth-rate, lineage, and many co-alteration contexts. ARID1A loss does not reproduce a comparable direct effect, including H6/R6 and SMARCA4-intact H39/R20, which helps distinguish a SMARCA4-specific association from a broad SWI/SNF claim. This is consistent with synthetic-lethal biology but does not prove mechanism.\n\n2. MSI-high is associated with stronger WRN dependency. H7/R7 gives +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819; validation R93 gives +0.805, interval +0.758 to +0.851. This is one of the largest and most reproducible dataset associations, also robust across technical and biological strata. The MSI-high by STK11-loss co-alteration stratum H278 is directionally supported but fragile because the exposed cell has only 22 observations; it should not be used as a main claim.\n\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency. The initially expected stronger-dependency hypothesis H8/R8 is rejected because the raw contrast is positive, meaning exposed KEAP1-loss cells are less negative. The accepted reframing H20/R8 gives +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816; validation R79 gives +0.829, interval +0.800 to +0.857. The magnitude is far above the practical reference near +0.009. Interpretation is that KEAP1-loss cells have much less NFE2L2 dependency in this dataset. This may reflect selection, co-alteration architecture, assay dependence, or dataset-specific configuration; it is not mechanistic proof.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. H17/R24 gives +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319; validation R66 gives +0.307, interval +0.228 to +0.387. This exceeds the practical reference near +0.028 and remains robust across multiple strata. The PTEN-by-TP53 interaction H158/R112 and its opposite H163/R133 do not support reliable effect modification, and the PTEN-by-library interaction H102/R119/R120 is discordant; therefore the simpler main PTEN association is more defensible.\n\n5. TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. H73/R37 gives +0.396, interval +0.325 to +0.467; validation R39 gives +0.382, interval +0.280 to +0.485. The finding identifies TP53-loss cells as having measurably less USP7 dependency, not greater dependency. It exceeds the practical reference near +0.018 and is stable across library, Cas9, screen-quality, lineage, media-serum, growth-rate, and co-alteration contexts.\n\n6. CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells is associated with stronger MDM2 dependency. H140/R88 gives +0.119, interval +0.079 to +0.158; validation R106 gives +0.112, interval +0.053 to +0.171. This exceeds the practical reference near +0.027 and is biologically plausible because MDM2 dependency may be more consequential when TP53 signaling remains potentially intact. The effect persists across many strata, but some conditional strata are less precise, and MTAP-specific analyses do not establish whether CDKN2A is the causal locus within the 9p21 region.\n\nThe six accepted core associations are supported by independent internal validation intervals within this supplied dataset. That validation strengthens confidence in the dataset-level associations but does not establish causality or external generalizability. The effects are so large relative to practical thresholds that multiplicity is unlikely to overturn them. Robustness checks, including male cells with adequate Cas9 activity H292-H297, reduce concern that the core associations are confined to one sex or to high- or low-quality screen strata.\n\nNegative and unsupported findings. Direct matched driver-dependency hypotheses are largely not supported in this dataset. BRAF V600E does not show meaningful stronger BRAF dependency in H1/R1 or in KRAS-negative cells in H222/R190. ERBB2 amplification does not show stronger ERBB2 dependency in H3/R3, including in EGFR-amplification-negative cells H223/R191. EGFR amplification is not a stable direct EGFR-dependency association: H2/R2 is rejected and validation R13 is small and inconsistent; KRAS-mutant or lineage-restricted EGFR amplification analyses remain unresolved. ARID1A loss does not support a direct stronger SMARCA2 dependency signal, including in SMARCA4-intact cells H39/R20. Broad MYC-amplification associations are not supported across USP7 H10/R10, POLR2A H13/R23, RPL11 H14/R121, KIF18A H111/R61, DHX9 H185/R149, STAT3 H191/R155, or TMED10 H229/R197. KRAS-mutation effects on KRAS dependency are unresolved and practically small overall, with H4/R4 and KRAS-subgroup analyses not yielding reliable clinically meaningful effects. STK11-loss main effects on KRAS and STAT3 dependencies are not supported where tested, and STK11-loss conditionals for USP7 under TP53-intact and TP53-loss status H298/R265 and H299/R266 are rejected. The mechanistic BRCA2-loss to KIF18A-dependency hypothesis H300/R267 is rejected. Some statistically significant small effects point opposite to hypothesized directions, such as certain DHX9 or WRN findings, but they are not clinically meaningful in the hypothesized direction and do not change the main report.\n\nInteractions and effect modification. Interaction analyses mostly do not add reliable biology beyond the six main associations. Lineage modifiers, library modifiers, TP53, MTAP, ARID1A, KRAS, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, and STAT3 modifier tests are usually null, underpowered, discordant, or below practical thresholds. H158/R112 and H163/R133 do not support robust TP53-loss modification of the PTEN-loss effect on STAT3 dependency. H102/R119/R120 does not support a reliable PTEN-by-library modification. H154/R108 and H155/R109 do not establish CDKN2A effect modification by TP53 or MTAP. H279/R246 provides no meaningful support for a CDKN2A-independent MTAP effect among CDKN2A-intact, TP53-intact cells. These nulls should be read as absence of demonstrated modification in this dataset, not proof of absence.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved uncertainty remains in smaller co-alteration contexts and low-power subgroups: KRAS-mutant co-alteration contexts for KRAS dependency, EGFR amplification within KRAS-mutant subgroups, EGFR-ERBB2 cross-talk, BRCA2-loss associations with DHX9, MTAP-only specificity, MDM2-STK11 co-alteration, the fragile WRN MSI-high STK11-loss stratum, and many closed unresolved subgroup effects. Wide intervals mean non-significance is not evidence of absence, and small significant effects should not be elevated above practical relevance without validation. Because the independent validation budget is exhausted, further internal uncertainty reduction by validation is not currently available.\n\nMost informative next analysis. The highest-value next analysis is a prespecified external replication of exactly the six core signed associations: SMARCA4 loss for stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high for stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss for weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss for stronger STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss for weaker USP7 dependency, and CDKN2A loss among TP53-intact cells for stronger MDM2 dependency. The replication should preserve the same exposure and comparator definitions, eligibility rules, signed directions, practical-effect thresholds, minimum cell-count rules, and screen-quality stratifications. If external replication is unavailable, future internal analyses should avoid broad subgroup fishing and be limited to a very small set of adequately powered high-prior conditional tests with independent replication, with special caution for small exposed co-alteration cells. If mechanistic interpretation is the goal, orthogonal experimental perturbations, such as targeted co-deletion or rescue and independent screens, would be more informative than further observational subgroup contrasts."}}

record.narrative:
With the independent validation budget exhausted and no discovery assessments due, this explore stage registers only a small, prespecified set of follow-up comparisons rather than broad subgroup fishing. The first two proposals address unresolved direct-driver hypotheses in contexts with higher biological prior. EGFR amplification is tested among adenocarcinoma samples with relatively high screen quality because a weak or inconsistent overall EGFR-amplification effect could reflect lineage mixing or technical noise; the registered claim is that EGFR-amplified cells have stronger EGFR dependency, corresponding to a negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast and therefore a positive controller-signed estimate under direction -1. A practically meaningful effect is approximately 0.025 dependency-score units, about 10% of the mean absolute EGFR dependency scale. KRAS mutation is tested in cells lacking TP53 and STK11 loss, a biologically simpler co-alteration background; the same reasoning applies, with a practical threshold near 0.024. Both tests remain dataset-only association tests and do not establish causality or therapeutic vulnerability.

The third proposal tests ARID1A co-loss within SMARCA4-loss cells for SMARCA2 dependency. The core SMARCA4-loss association is extremely strong, but ARID1A loss as a main predictor is not supported. This comparison asks whether ARID1A co-alteration further amplifies the SMARCA2 dependency signal specifically in the SMARCA4-deficient synthetic-lethal context. The expected raw direction is negative, and a clinically meaningful practical threshold is roughly 0.042 given the larger SMARCA2 dependency scale. Because prior interaction evidence was modest, this may well be null or subthreshold; nullity would not refute the accepted SMARCA4-specific association but would reduce support for an additional ARID1A effect within SMARCA4-deficient cells.

The fourth proposal tests the accepted CDKN2A-loss association with stronger MDM2 dependency among TP53-intact cells that also lack MYC amplification. This tests whether the core MDM2 finding remains meaningful independent of MYC co-amplification, a common and potentially confounding genomic state. The expected raw direction remains negative, signed to positive under direction -1, with a practical threshold near 0.027. This is not a new mechanism claim; it is an internal specificity/robustness test. If all four estimates have valid cells with at least 20 observations per comparison cell and signed lower bounds exceeding practical thresholds, they would strengthen context-specific support. If unresolved, that means insufficient evidence in the tested stratum, not absence of an effect. No new validation is requested because no independent validation remains.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
